properties.key: A stable name for the control. Lists use it to keep each item's state when items move, and it stays the same across updates.
properties.data: Any value you attach to the control, such as an id; read it back in handlers with `event.control.props["data"]`.
properties.label: Text label shown for the control.
properties.content: The single child control rendered inside this control.
properties.title: The control shown as the title.
properties.subtitle: The control shown as the secondary line below the title.
properties.leading: Control placed before the main content (e.g. an icon or avatar).
properties.trailing: Control placed after the main content.
properties.actions: Controls shown in the trailing action area.
properties.icon: Icon name shown by the control.
properties.src: Source URL or asset path of the image.
properties.url: URL the control loads or links to.
properties.options: The selectable options (built with the control's option helper).
properties.disabled: Disables the control and every control inside it: they stop reacting to input and stop sending events.
properties.visible: Hides the control when false; a hidden control takes no space.
properties.divisions: Number of discrete steps between min and max.
properties.hint_text: Placeholder shown when the field is empty.
properties.helper_text: Helper text shown below the field.
properties.error_text: Error message shown below the field; also marks it invalid.
properties.password: Obscures the entered text when true.
properties.multiline: Allows multiple lines of input when true.
properties.read_only: Prevents editing while still allowing selection.
properties.clip_behavior: How content overflowing the bounds is clipped.
properties.expand: Inside a `row`, a `column` or the page, fills the free space along the parent's main axis. `true` is a share of 1; an integer sets the share, so `expand: 2` gets twice the space of `expand: 1`. [Sizing](/docs/controls-and-layout#sizing) lists the parents that use it.
properties.expand_loose: With `expand`, lets the control stay smaller than its share instead of filling it.
properties.padding: Inner spacing between the border and the content.
properties.margin: Space around the control, in logical pixels: one number for every side, or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`, where a side you leave out is 0. [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the `all:` shorthand Ruflet main adds.
properties.align: Aligns the control in the space its parent gives it, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (`{ x: 0, y: 0 }` is the center). [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the names Ruflet main adds, such as `"top_left"`.
properties.alignment: Alignment of the content within the control.
properties.aspect_ratio: Keeps the control at this width-to-height ratio, for example `16 / 9.0`.
properties.col: Columns the control spans in its parent `responsive_row`: a number, or a hash per breakpoint such as `{ "xs" => 12, "md" => 6 }` (default: all of them). Other parents ignore it.
properties.top: Distance from the top edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.bottom: Distance from the bottom edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.left: Distance from the left edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.right: Distance from the right edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.rotate: Rotates the control clockwise by an angle in radians, such as `Math::PI / 4`, or by `{ angle:, alignment: }` to turn it around another point. Its parent still lays it out unrotated.
properties.scale: Scales the control: `1` is its normal size and `0.5` half of it. `{ scale_x:, scale_y: }` scales each axis on its own.
properties.offset: Moves the control by a fraction of its own size, as `{ x:, y: }`: `{ x: 1, y: 0 }` shifts it one width to the right. Its parent still lays it out at the original place.
properties.rtl: Lays the control out right to left when true.
properties.adaptive: Accepted for Flet compatibility; no Ruflet client reads it. The design always follows the platform: Cupertino widgets on iOS and macOS, Material widgets everywhere else.
properties.tooltip: Text shown when the user hovers over the control or long-presses it.
properties.badge: A badge on the control's corner: a String or number shown as its label, such as `"3"`, or `badge(...)` for a styled one.
properties.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown when hovering the control.
properties.animate_opacity: Animates changes to `opacity`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_size: Animates changes to `width` and `height`, or to the content's own size when neither is set: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_scale: Animates changes to `scale`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_rotation: Animates changes to `rotate`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_offset: Animates changes to `offset`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_position: Animates changes to `left`, `top`, `right` and `bottom` inside a `stack`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_margin: Animates changes to `margin`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.animate_align: Animates changes to `align`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
properties.size_change_interval: Minimum time between two `on_size_change` events, in milliseconds (default 10).
properties.action: A client action, built with `Ruflet.client_action`, that the client runs inside the tap before it sends `on_click`. Use it for work browsers allow only during a user gesture, such as opening a link, copying to the clipboard or picking files.
properties.spacing: Space between the control's children, or between its parts such as a checkbox and its label, in logical pixels.
properties.run_spacing: Space between lines of children when they wrap, in logical pixels.
properties.tight: Takes only as much space along the main axis as the children need.
properties.reverse: Reverses the direction: lists start from the end, and animations play backwards.
properties.horizontal: Lays the items out and scrolls them horizontally instead of vertically.
properties.scroll: Makes the content scrollable when it overflows: `"auto"`, `"adaptive"`, `"always"` or `"hidden"` (no scrollbar).
properties.scroll_interval: Minimum time between `on_scroll` events, in milliseconds (default 10).
properties.auto_scroll: Scrolls to the end automatically whenever the children change, as in a chat or log view.
properties.auto_scroll_animation: How `auto_scroll` moves to the end: a duration in milliseconds, `{ duration:, curve: }`, or `false` to jump.
properties.keyboard_dismiss_behavior: Whether scrolling closes the on-screen keyboard: `"manual"` (default) or `"onDrag"`.
properties.end_reached_threshold: How close to the end, in logical pixels, the user must scroll before `on_end_reached` fires (default 200).
properties.item_extent: Size of each item along the scroll direction, in logical pixels, such as the row height of a picker wheel.
properties.cache_extent: How far beyond the visible area, in logical pixels, the list builds items ahead of time.
properties.build_controls_on_demand: Builds only the children that are scrolled into view (default `true`).
properties.semantic_child_count: Number of items screen readers announce for the list.
properties.divider_thickness: Thickness of the dividers drawn between items or rows, in logical pixels.
properties.first_item_prototype: Uses the first item to measure the size of every item, which speeds up layout.
properties.prototype_item: A sample item used to measure the size of every item.
properties.show_default_drag_handles: Shows the platform drag handle on each item; set `false` to drag only by your own `reorderable_drag_handle`.
properties.auto_scroller_velocity_scalar: How fast the list scrolls while an item is dragged near its edge.
properties.anchor: Relative position, from 0.0 to 1.0, of the zero scroll offset in the viewport.
properties.selected_index: Index of the selected item, starting at 0.
properties.size: Size of the control: a number in logical pixels for icons, text and indicators, or a size name such as `"small"` or `"large"` for buttons.
properties.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button.
properties.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the control fades to while it is pressed.
properties.icon_size: Size of the icon, in logical pixels.
properties.gradient: Gradient that fills the control instead of a solid color.
properties.blend_mode: How the control's color or shader is combined with what is behind it, for example `"multiply"` or `"srcIn"`.
properties.border_side: Border line, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`.
properties.fit: How the content is sized into the available space: a box fit such as `"contain"` or `"cover"` for images and animations, a stack fit such as `"expand"` for stacks.
properties.repeat: Repeats the content: loops an animation, or tiles an image (`"repeat"`, `"repeatX"`, `"repeatY"`).
properties.x: Horizontal position: in logical pixels on a canvas, or the data value on the x axis in a chart.
properties.y: Vertical position: in logical pixels on a canvas, or the data value on the y axis in a chart.
properties.paint: How a canvas shape is drawn (color, stroke width, fill or stroke, gradient), built with `paint(...)`.
properties.semantics_label: Text that screen readers announce for the control.
properties.semantics_value: Value that screen readers announce, such as a progress percentage.
properties.exclude_from_semantics: Hides the control from screen readers; on a gesture detector, hides its gestures.
properties.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space.
properties.direction: Layout direction of the segments: `"horizontal"` (default) or `"vertical"`.
properties.variant: Style variant of the control, for example `"elevated"`, `"filled"` or `"outlined"` for a card.
properties.label_position: Side of the control the label is placed on: `"right"` (default) or `"left"`.
properties.toggleable: Lets a second tap clear the selection.
properties.default: Marks the action as the default one; iOS shows it in bold.
properties.destructive: Marks the action as destructive; iOS shows it in red.
properties.modal: When true, tapping outside the dialog or sheet does not close it.
properties.scrollable: Lets the content scroll when it does not fit.
properties.maintain_state: Keeps the hidden children alive while the control is collapsed.
properties.extended: Shows each label beside its icon instead of under it.
properties.label_type: Which destination labels are shown: `"all"`, `"selected"` or `"none"`.
properties.group_alignment: How the groups of items are aligned.
properties.use_indicator: Draws a highlight behind the selected destination.
properties.indicator_shape: Shape of the highlight behind the selected destination.
properties.min_width: Minimum width of the control, in logical pixels.
properties.min_extended_width: Width of the rail when `extended` is true.
properties.duration: Length of the control's animation, or how long it stays visible, in milliseconds.
properties.reverse_duration: Length of the animation for the outgoing content, in milliseconds.
properties.animation_duration: Length of the control's transition animation, in milliseconds.
properties.animation_curve: Easing curve of the control's transition animation, for example `"easeInOut"`.
properties.switch_in_curve: Easing curve for the incoming content, for example `"easeOut"`.
properties.switch_out_curve: Easing curve for the outgoing content, for example `"easeIn"`.
properties.transition: Animation between the old and the new content: `"fade"` (default), `"scale"` or `"rotation"`.
properties.animating: Runs the animation while true; set `false` to pause it.
properties.animation: Animation applied when the chart data changes: a duration in milliseconds or `{ duration:, curve: }`.
properties.begin: Value the transition animation starts from.
properties.end: Value the transition animation ends at.
properties.curve: Easing curve of the animation, for example `"easeInOut"`.
properties.delay: Time to wait before the animation starts, in milliseconds.
properties.sliding: Selects the sliding iOS segmented control; set by `cupertino_sliding_segmented_button`.
properties.interval: Time between sensor readings, in milliseconds.
properties.enabled: Turns the sensor stream on or off.
properties.cancel_on_error: Stops the sensor stream after the first error.
properties.interactive: Enables touch tooltips and highlights on the chart (default `true`).
properties.min_x: Smallest value shown on the x axis.
properties.max_x: Largest value shown on the x axis.
properties.min_y: Smallest value shown on the y axis.
properties.max_y: Largest value shown on the y axis.
properties.left_axis: Axis drawn on the left of the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.right_axis: Axis drawn on the right of the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.top_axis: Axis drawn above the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.bottom_axis: Axis drawn below the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.show_tooltip: Shows the tooltip for this data point.
properties.capitalization: Automatic capitalization of typed text: `"none"`, `"words"`, `"sentences"` or `"characters"`.
properties.text_align: Horizontal alignment of the text: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`, `"justify"`, `"start"` or `"end"`.
properties.text_size: Font size of the typed text.
properties.text_vertical_align: Vertical position of the text in a tall field, from -1.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom).
properties.error: Error shown below the field, as text or a control; it also marks the field invalid.
properties.helper: Helper text or control shown below the field.
properties.counter: Text or control shown below the field on the right, often a character count.
properties.prefix: Text or control shown inside the field before the input.
properties.suffix: Text or control shown inside the field after the input.
properties.collapsed: Removes the field's decoration and padding for a minimal input.
properties.align_label_with_hint: Aligns the label with the hint text; useful for multiline fields.
properties.fit_parent_size: Makes the field fill its parent's size.
properties.hint_fade_duration: Time the hint takes to fade when the user starts typing, in milliseconds.
properties.error_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of error text.
properties.helper_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of helper text.
properties.hint_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of hint text.
properties.max_length: Maximum number of characters the user can enter; a counter shows the count.
properties.max_lines: Maximum number of lines the control shows.
properties.min_lines: Minimum number of lines the field shows.
properties.input_filter: Limits which characters can be typed, with a regular expression.
properties.autofill_hints: Hints for the platform's autofill, for example `["email"]`.
properties.can_reveal_password: Shows an eye button that reveals a `password` field's text.
properties.obscuring_character: Character shown in place of each typed character in a `password` field.
properties.shift_enter: In a multiline field, Enter submits and Shift+Enter starts a new line.
properties.can_request_focus: Whether the field can take keyboard focus.
properties.always_call_on_tap: Fires `on_click` on every tap, even when the field already has focus.
properties.enable_interactive_selection: Lets the user select text and use copy and paste.
properties.enable_ime_personalized_learning: Lets the keyboard learn from what the user types.
properties.enable_stylus_handwriting: Allows handwriting input with a stylus where the platform supports it.
properties.ignore_up_down_keys: Ignores the up and down arrow keys in the field.
properties.keyboard_brightness: Appearance of the iOS keyboard: `"light"` or `"dark"`.
properties.smart_dashes_type: Turns iOS smart dashes on or off.
properties.smart_quotes_type: Turns iOS smart quotes on or off.
properties.shadows: Drop shadows painted behind the control.
properties.text_input_action: The keyboard's action button, such as `"next"`, `"search"` or `"done"`.
properties.placeholder_text: Prompt shown while the field is empty (Cupertino look only; `hint_text` takes precedence).
properties.clear_button_visibility_mode: When the clear button shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`.
properties.clear_button_semantics_label: Label screen readers announce for the clear button.
properties.locale: Locale for month and day names, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`.
properties.first_date: Earliest date the user can pick.
properties.last_date: Latest date the user can pick.
properties.entry_mode: How the value is entered, for example `"calendar"` or `"input"` for dates and `"dial"` or `"input"` for times.
properties.minute_interval: Step between selectable minutes, for example 5.
properties.allow_multiple_selection: Lets more than one segment be selected.
properties.allow_empty_selection: Lets the user clear the selection.
properties.round: Number of decimal places shown in the value label.
properties.suggestions: The suggestions the user can pick from.
properties.suggestions_max_height: Maximum height of the suggestion list, in logical pixels.
properties.menu_position: Where the menu opens relative to the button: `"over"` or `"under"`.
properties.foreground_image_src: Image drawn over the avatar's content, usually the user's photo.
properties.background_image_src: Image drawn behind the avatar's content.
properties.background: Control shown behind the content while it is swiped from start to end (right, or down); also used for the other direction when `secondary_background` is not set.
properties.secondary_background: Control shown behind the content while it is swiped from end to start (left, or up).
properties.dismiss_direction: Which swipes dismiss the control: `"horizontal"`, `"endToStart"`, `"startToEnd"`, `"vertical"`, `"up"`, `"down"` or `"none"`.
properties.dismiss_thresholds: Fraction of the width or height the control must travel before it is dismissed, per direction.
properties.movement_duration: Time the control takes to slide away or back, in milliseconds (default 200).
properties.resize_duration: Time the space left by a dismissed control takes to close, in milliseconds (default 300).
properties.cross_axis_end_offset: Moves the control across the swipe direction, as a fraction of its size, as it is dismissed.
properties.drag_interval: Minimum time between drag update events, in milliseconds.
properties.hover_interval: Minimum time between hover events, in milliseconds.
properties.multi_tap_touches: Number of fingers that `on_multi_tap` waits for.
properties.allowed_devices: Pointer kinds that can start a gesture, for example `["touch", "mouse"]`.
properties.trackpad_scroll_causes_scale: Treats two-finger trackpad scrolling as a pinch.
properties.sort_column_index: Index of the column that shows the sort arrow.
properties.sort_ascending: Direction of the sort arrow: `true` for ascending.
properties.show_checkbox_column: Adds a checkbox column for selecting rows.
properties.show_bottom_border: Draws a border below the last row.
properties.column_spacing: Space between columns, in logical pixels.
properties.horizontal_margin: Space before the first and after the last column, in logical pixels.
properties.checkbox_horizontal_margin: Space around the row checkboxes, in logical pixels.
properties.horizontal_lines: Border line between rows, for example `{ color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.vertical_lines: Border line between columns, for example `{ color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.data_row_min_height: Minimum height of a data row, in logical pixels.
properties.data_row_max_height: Maximum height of a data row, in logical pixels.
properties.heading_row_height: Height of the heading row, in logical pixels.
properties.viewport_fraction: Share of the viewport each page fills; below 1.0 the neighbouring pages show at the edges.
properties.pad_ends: Adds space before the first and after the last page when `viewport_fraction` is below 1.0.
properties.snap: Snaps to a resting position, such as a whole page, when the user stops dragging.
properties.keep_page: Restores the current page when the page view is rebuilt.
properties.implicit_scrolling: Lets assistive technology move to the next and previous page.
properties.force_actions_below: Puts the actions under the message instead of beside it.
properties.notch_margin: Space between the floating action button and the notch, in logical pixels.
properties.full_screen: Opens the search view full screen.
properties.shrink_wrap: Sizes the control to its content instead of filling the available space.
properties.bar_elevation: Shadow depth of the search bar.
properties.bar_leading: Control shown at the start of the search bar.
properties.bar_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the search bar.
properties.bar_size_constraints: Size limits of the search bar.
properties.view_elevation: Shadow depth of the search view.
properties.view_leading: Control shown at the start of the search view's header.
properties.view_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the search view's header.
properties.view_size_constraints: Size limits of the search view.
properties.year_2023: Uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.
properties.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the track, in logical pixels.
properties.affinity: Where the expand icon sits: `"leading"`, `"trailing"` or `"platform"`.
properties.collapsed_shape: Shape of the tile while collapsed.
properties.unit_id: Your AdMob ad unit ID; without it the client loads Google's test ad unit.
properties.request: Targeting options for the ad request, such as keywords.
properties.active_thumb_image_src: Image drawn on the thumb while the switch is on.
properties.inactive_thumb_image_src: Image drawn on the thumb while the switch is off.
properties.item_count: Number of items in the indicator, for variants that draw several.
properties.wave_type: Where the wave starts for wave variants: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`.
properties.horizontal_grid_lines: Horizontal grid lines across the chart, for example `{ interval: 10, color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.vertical_grid_lines: Vertical grid lines across the chart, for example `{ interval: 1, color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.baseline_x: x value the chart draws from.
properties.baseline_y: y value the chart draws from, such as the bottom of the bars.
properties.coordinates: Position on the map as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`; a list of positions for lines and shapes.
properties.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40).
properties.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull on iOS to start a refresh.
properties.refresh_timeout: Longest time, in milliseconds, the refresh indicator waits for `on_refresh` (default 30 seconds).
properties.enable_alpha: Lets the user pick a transparency value as well as a color.
properties.prefix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits for the prefix icon.
properties.suffix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits for the suffix icon.
properties.show_drag_handle: Shows a drag handle at the top of the sheet.
properties.automatically_imply_leading: Adds a back or menu button automatically when the page has somewhere to go back to or a drawer.
properties.transition_between_routes: Animates the bar between pages on iOS.
properties.previous_page_title: Title of the previous page, shown next to the iOS back button.
properties.tristate: Allows a third, mixed state: `value` may be `nil`, drawn as a dash. A tap then cycles unchecked, checked, mixed (default false).
properties.show_checkmark: Shows a check mark on the chip while it is selected (default true).
properties.delete_icon: Control shown as the delete button, in place of the default cross. It appears only when the chip has an `on_delete` handler.
properties.delete_icon_tooltip: Tooltip of the delete button, which screen readers also announce.
properties.dispose_action: What the platform does with the entered data when the group is removed: `"commit"` (default) offers to save it to the autofill service, `"cancel"` discards it.
properties.active_thumb_image: The `cupertino_switch` spelling of `active_thumb_image_src`: image drawn on the thumb while the switch is on.
properties.inactive_thumb_image: The `cupertino_switch` spelling of `inactive_thumb_image_src`: image drawn on the thumb while the switch is off.
properties.active_track_color: Color of the track while the switch is on.
properties.inactive_track_color: Color of the track while the switch is off.
properties.inactive_thumb_color: Color of the thumb while the switch is off.
properties.thumb_icon: Icon drawn on the thumb, for example `"check"`.
properties.track_outline_width: Width of the track's outline, in logical pixels.
properties.diameter_ratio: How curved the wheel looks: the ratio of its diameter to its height (default 1.07). Smaller values curve it more. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.looping: Lets the wheel wrap around, so the first item follows the last (default false). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.magnification: Zoom applied to the item in the selection band (default 1.0); it takes effect with `use_magnifier: true`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.use_magnifier: Magnifies the item in the selection band by `magnification` (default false). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.off_axis_fraction: Tilts the wheel sideways, as a fraction of its width; 0.0 (default) looks straight on. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.squeeze: How tightly the items are packed on the wheel (default 1.45); higher values fit more items. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.selection_overlay: Control drawn over the selected row, in place of the default rounded band. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.default_selection_overlay_bgcolor: Color of the default rounded band behind the selected row. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.date_order: Order of the day, month and year wheels: `"dmy"`, `"mdy"`, `"ymd"` or `"ydm"`. By default it follows the locale. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.minimum_year: Earliest year the year wheel offers (default 1); `first_date` limits it further. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.maximum_year: Latest year the year wheel offers; by default it has no limit other than `last_date`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.show_day_of_week: Shows the weekday next to the day, for example "Mon 15" (default false). Only the date mode shows it. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.use_24h_format: Shows the time wheels in 24-hour format instead of with AM and PM (default false). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.second_interval: Step between the seconds the picker offers, for example 5 (default 1). Use a number that divides 60.
properties.interaction: How the user can move the thumb: `"tapAndSlide"` (default), `"tapOnly"`, `"slideOnly"` or `"slideThumb"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.secondary_track_value: A second position marked on the track, between `min` and `max`, for example how much of a video has loaded. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.secondary_active_color: Color of the track up to `secondary_track_value`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.elevation_on_click: Shadow depth of the chip while it is pressed. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.leading_size_constraints: Size limits of the `leading` control, for example `{ max_width: 24, max_height: 24 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.delete_icon_size_constraints: Size limits of the delete button, for example `{ max_width: 24, max_height: 24 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.delete_icon_color: Color of the default delete icon. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.selected_shadow_color: Color of the chip's shadow while it is selected. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.enable_animation_style: Duration and curve of the animation when the chip is enabled or disabled, for example `{ duration: 300 }` (milliseconds). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.select_animation_style: Duration and curve of the selection animation, for example `{ duration: 300 }` (milliseconds). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.leading_drawer_animation_style: Duration and curve of the animation that shows and hides `leading`, for example `{ duration: 300 }` (milliseconds). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.delete_drawer_animation_style: Duration and curve of the animation that shows and hides the delete button, for example `{ duration: 300 }` (milliseconds). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.click_color: Color of a segment while it is pressed. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.unselected_color: Background color of the segments that are not selected. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.editable: Lets the user type into the field (default false); `on_text_change` reports the text.
properties.enable_filter: While the user types in an `editable` dropdown, shows only the options whose text contains the typed text (default false). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.enable_search: While the user types in an `editable` dropdown, highlights the first option that matches the typed text (default true). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.expanded_insets: Makes the field as wide as its parent, minus these insets, for example `{ left: 16, right: 16 }`; `expand: true` alone gives zero insets. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.selected_suffix: Control shown after the selected option's text, for example a badge.
properties.selected_trailing_icon: Icon shown at the end of the field while the menu is open, in place of `trailing_icon`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.leading_icon: Icon or control shown at the start.
properties.menu_height: Maximum height of the open menu, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.menu_width: Width of the open menu, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.menu_border_radius: Corner radius of the open menu; `border_radius` rounds the field itself.
properties.hour_format: How hours are shown: `"h12"` with AM and PM, `"h24"`, or `"system"` (the default), which follows the device setting. iOS and macOS show 24 hours only for `"h24"`, in a browser too.
properties.orientation: Layout of the clock dialog: `"portrait"` or `"landscape"`. By default it follows the screen. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.hour_label_text: Label under the hour field in the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.minute_label_text: Label under the minute field in the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.switch_to_input_icon: Icon of the button that switches the dialog to text input. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.switch_to_calendar_icon: Icon of the button that switches the dialog back to the calendar. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.switch_to_timer_icon: Icon of the button that switches the dialog back to the clock dial. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.error_format_text: Error shown when the typed date does not match the expected format. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.error_invalid_text: Error shown when the typed value is outside the allowed range. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.error_invalid_range_text: Error shown when the typed end date is before the start date. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.field_hint_text: Hint in the date field of the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.field_label_text: Label of the date field in the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.field_start_hint_text: Hint in the start-date field of the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.field_end_hint_text: Hint in the end-date field of the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.field_start_label_text: Label of the start-date field in the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.field_end_label_text: Label of the end-date field in the dialog's input mode. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.save_text: Label of the save button of the full-screen range dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.help_text: Title shown at the top of the picker.
properties.confirm_text: Label of the button that confirms the choice; iOS and macOS show "Done" by default, in a browser too.
properties.inline: Draws the picker where you add it, instead of as a dialog that `page.show_dialog` opens (default false).
properties.mode: Which wheels the picker shows: `"hms"` (hours, minutes and seconds; the default), `"hm"` or `"ms"`. `cupertino_timer_picker` sends `"hour_minute_seconds"`, which clients read as `"hms"`.
properties.cursor_height: Height of the text cursor, in logical pixels.
properties.cursor_width: Width of the text cursor, in logical pixels (default 2).
properties.cursor_radius: Corner radius of the text cursor, in logical pixels.
properties.cursor_error_color: Color of the text cursor while the field shows an error. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.animate_cursor_opacity: Fades the text cursor in and out instead of blinking it. By default iOS and macOS fade it and other platforms blink it; a browser follows the device it runs on.
properties.selection_color: Color of the highlight behind selected text.
properties.strut_style: Minimum line height and spacing for the typed text.
properties.scroll_padding: Space kept between the field and the screen edges when it scrolls into view: a number for every side, or a `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }` map (default 20).
properties.focused_color: Color of the typed text while the field has focus.
properties.focused_bgcolor: Background color while the field has focus.
properties.focused_border_color: Border color while the field has focus.
properties.focused_border_width: Border width while the field has focus, in logical pixels.
properties.placeholder_style: Style of the `placeholder_text`, for example `{ color: "#9ca3af" }`; `hint_style` wins when both are set. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.hint_style: Style of the `hint_text`, for example `{ color: "#9ca3af" }`.
properties.prefix_style: Style of `prefix` when it is text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.suffix_style: Style of `suffix` when it is text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.helper_style: Style of the helper text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.counter_style: Style of the counter text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.prefix_icon: Icon shown inside the field, before the text and the `prefix`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.suffix_icon: Icon shown inside the field, after the text and the `suffix`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.label_style: Style of the label, for example `{ size: 14, color: "#6b7280" }`.
properties.bar_bgcolor: Background color of the search bar.
properties.bar_hint_text: Hint shown in the search bar while it is empty.
properties.bar_hint_text_style: Style of `bar_hint_text`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.bar_text_style: Style of the text typed in the bar. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.bar_overlay_color: Highlight color of the bar while it is pressed, hovered or focused. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.bar_padding: Space inside the bar around its content, for example `{ left: 16, right: 16 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.bar_scroll_padding: Space kept between the bar and the screen edges when it scrolls into view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.bar_shadow_color: Color of the bar's shadow. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_bgcolor: Background color of the open search view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_bar_padding: Space around the search field in the open view's header. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_header_height: Height of the open view's header, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_header_text_style: Style of the text typed in the open view's header. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_hint_text: Hint shown in the open view's header while it is empty. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_hint_text_style: Style of `view_hint_text`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.view_padding: Space around the open view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
properties.message: Smaller text below the title, as a string or a control.
properties.cancel: An `action_sheet_action` set apart below the other actions, for closing the sheet without choosing one.
properties.application_name: Name of the app, shown as the dialog title. Without it the dialog uses the app's window title.
properties.application_version: Version shown next to the app name, for example `"2.1.0"`.
properties.application_legalese: Small print shown in the dialog and on the licenses page, such as a copyright notice.
properties.application_icon: Control shown as the app's icon, usually an `icon` or an `image`.
properties.view: `"about"` (default) opens the about dialog; `"licenses"` opens the open-source licenses page directly, as a full page instead of a dialog.
properties.bar_height: Thickness of the bar, in logical pixels (default 4; 3 on iOS and macOS).
properties.stop_indicator_color: Color of the dot at the end of the track. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
properties.stop_indicator_radius: Radius of the dot at the end of the track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
properties.placeholder: A control shown in place of the content while it loads.
properties.show_edit_icon: Shows a pencil icon in the cell to tell users they can edit it; handle the cell's `on_tap` to start editing.
properties.cells: The `data_cell` controls of the row, one per column; the first positional argument sets them.
properties.heading_row_alignment: How the heading is aligned in its cell: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`.
properties.fixed_width: Fixed width of the column, in logical pixels; it replaces the `size` share.
properties.specific_row_height: Height of this row, in logical pixels, instead of the table's `data_row_height`.
properties.data_row_height: Height of every data row, in logical pixels.
properties.bottom_margin: Space below the last row, in logical pixels (default 0).
properties.empty: Control shown in place of the rows while the table has none.
properties.fixed_left_columns: Number of columns at the start that stay in place while the table scrolls sideways (default 0).
properties.fixed_top_rows: Number of rows at the top, the heading row included, that stay in place while the table scrolls (default 1).
properties.fixed_columns_color: Background color of the fixed columns.
properties.fixed_corner_color: Background color of the corner where the fixed rows and fixed columns meet.
properties.lm_ratio: Width of an `"l"` column relative to an `"m"` column (default 1.2).
properties.sm_ratio: Width of an `"s"` column relative to an `"m"` column (default 0.67).
properties.heading_row_decoration: Box decoration of the heading row, for example `{ bgcolor: "#f1f5f9", border_radius: 8 }`.
properties.heading_checkbox_theme: Checkbox theme of the heading checkbox: `{ fill_color:, check_color:, border_side:, shape: }`.
properties.data_row_checkbox_theme: Checkbox theme of the row checkboxes: `{ fill_color:, check_color:, border_side:, shape: }`.
properties.show_heading_checkbox: Shows the select-all checkbox in the heading row while `show_checkbox_column` is on (default true).
properties.checkbox_alignment: Alignment of the checkboxes in their column, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0 (centered by default).
properties.sort_arrow_animation_duration: Length of the sort arrow's turn animation, in milliseconds.
properties.sort_arrow_icon: Icon used for the sort arrow (default `"arrow_upward"`).
properties.visible_horizontal_scroll_bar: Keeps the horizontal scroll bar visible while the table can scroll sideways.
properties.visible_vertical_scroll_bar: Keeps the vertical scroll bar visible while the table can scroll up and down.
properties.can_tap_header: Lets a tap anywhere on the header toggle the panel, not only on the arrow button (default false). iOS and macOS ignore it: the whole header always toggles the panel there.
properties.additional_divider_margin: Extra inset of the dividers on top of `divider_margin`, so they start after leading icons (default 56 on Android, web, Windows and Linux and 44 on iOS and macOS when `has_leading` is true, 0 otherwise).
properties.divider_margin: Inset of the dividers between rows from the section's leading edge, in logical pixels (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 20 on iOS and macOS).
properties.has_leading: Tells the section that its rows have leading icons, so the dividers start after them (default true).
properties.top_margin: Extra space above the section, in logical pixels (default 0; 22 on iOS and macOS for the `"base"` variant).
properties.separator_color: Color of the dividers between rows.
properties.column_widths: Widths per column index: `{ 0 => { type: "flex", value: 2 } }`, where `type` is `"flex"`, `"fixed"`, `"fraction"` or `"intrinsic"`; a bare number is a fixed width.
properties.default_column_width: Width of the columns missing from `column_widths`, in the same form (default: equal flex shares).
properties.inner_borders: Also draws lines between the rows and columns when `border_color` is set (default true).
properties.default_vertical_alignment: Vertical position of the cells in their row: `"top"` (default), `"middle"`, `"bottom"`, `"baseline"` or `"fill"`.
properties.center_title: Centers the title in the bar. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; iOS and macOS ignore it and place the title the iOS way.
properties.foreground_decoration: Decoration painted over the content: `{ bgcolor:, gradient:, border:, border_radius:, shadows:, image:, shape:, blend_mode: }`.

events.on_click: Fired when the control is clicked/tapped.
events.on_change_start: Fired when the user starts changing the value.
events.on_change_end: Fired when the user finishes changing the value.
events.on_submit: Fired when the user submits the field, for example with the keyboard's done key; `event.data` is the text.
events.on_focus: Fired when the control gains focus.
events.on_blur: Fired when the control loses focus.
events.on_hover: Fired when the pointer enters/leaves the control.
events.on_tap_down: Fired when a pointer presses down; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point and `event.kind` the device, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`.
events.on_tap_cancel: Fired when a tap is cancelled.
events.on_tap_outside: Fired when a tap occurs outside the control.
events.on_dismiss: Fired when the control is dismissed: a dialog, sheet, menu, picker or banner closes, or the user swipes a dismissible away.
events.on_scroll: Fired when the scroll position changes.
events.on_select: Fired when the user picks an item; what `event.data` holds depends on the control, see its page.
events.on_selection_change: Fired when the user changes the selected text; `event.data` describes the new selection.
events.on_state_change: Fired when the control's state changes.
events.on_enter: Fired when the pointer enters the control.
events.on_exit: Fired when the pointer leaves the control.
events.on_image_error: Fired when an image the control shows fails to load; `event.data` describes the failure.
events.on_loaded: Fired when the control has loaded.
events.on_visible: Fired when the control appears on screen.
events.on_resize: Fired when the control is resized.
events.on_animation_end: Fired when an `animate_*` animation finishes. `event.data` names the animation: `"opacity"`, `"rotation"`, `"scale"`, `"offset"`, `"align"`, `"margin"` or `"position"`; a container's own `animate` reports `"container"`.
events.on_size_change: Fired after the control's size changes, at most once per `size_change_interval`. `event.data` is `{ w: width, h: height }` in logical pixels.
events.on_action_result: Fired when a client `action:` has finished; the event carries its result or error.
events.on_end_reached: Fired when the user scrolls within `end_reached_threshold` of the end, for loading more items. It fires once, then again after the content grows (you added items) or after the user scrolls back more than twice `end_reached_threshold` from the end. `event.data` has the keys `:pixels`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`.
events.on_refresh: Fired when the user pulls down to refresh; the indicator spins until the handler returns.
events.on_paste_files: Fired when the user pastes files into the field; `event.files` lists them.
events.on_tap_outside_view: Fired when the user taps outside the open search view.
events.on_tap_outside_bar: Fired when the user taps outside the search bar.
events.on_reading: Fired with each new sensor reading in `event.data`.
events.on_event: Fired on chart or map touch and pointer events; `event.data` describes the event.
events.on_load: Fired when the content has loaded.
events.on_cancel: Fired when the menu closes without a choice.
events.on_impression: Fired when the ad is shown to the user.
events.on_will_dismiss: Fired just before a screen the ad opened closes.
events.on_paid: Fired when the ad earns revenue; `event.data` holds the value and currency.
events.on_reorder: Fired when an item is dropped in a new position; `event.old_index` and `event.new_index` give the move.
events.on_reorder_start: Fired when the user starts dragging an item.
events.on_reorder_end: Fired when the user drops a dragged item.
events.on_confirm_dismiss: Fired before the control is dismissed. Reply with `page.invoke(event.control, "confirm_dismiss", args: { dismiss: true })`, or `dismiss: false` to keep it; without a reply the client cancels the dismissal after five minutes.
events.on_update: Fired while the control is dragged, with the direction and progress.
events.on_select_all: Fired when the user taps the select-all checkbox in the heading row; `event.data` is `true` to select every row and `nil` to clear them. Without this handler the table calls each row's `on_select_change` instead.
events.on_select_change: Fired when the user selects or clears the row; `event.data` is `true` when it is selected and `nil` when it is cleared. The row does not change by itself: set its `selected` with `page.update`.
events.on_sort: Fired when the user taps the column heading to sort; `event.data[:ci]` is the column index and `event.data[:asc]` the new direction.
events.on_tap_up: Fired when a pointer that pressed down lifts.
events.on_pan_start: Fired when a drag in any direction starts.
events.on_pan_update: Fired as a drag moves; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update.
events.on_pan_end: Fired when a drag ends; the event carries the velocity.
events.on_horizontal_drag_start: Fired when a horizontal drag starts.
events.on_horizontal_drag_update: Fired as a horizontal drag moves.
events.on_horizontal_drag_end: Fired when a horizontal drag ends.
events.on_vertical_drag_start: Fired when a vertical drag starts.
events.on_vertical_drag_update: Fired as a vertical drag moves.
events.on_vertical_drag_end: Fired when a vertical drag ends.
events.on_scale_start: Fired when a pinch or two-finger rotation starts.
events.on_scale_update: Fired as a pinch or rotation changes.
events.on_scale_end: Fired when a pinch or rotation ends.
events.on_entry_mode_change: Fired when the user switches the dialog between its picker and text input; `event.data[:entry_mode]` (a Symbol key) is the new mode, such as `"input"`. iOS and macOS never send it, in a browser too.
events.on_upload: Fired with the progress of a file upload.
events.on_color_change: Fired when the user picks a color; `event.data` is the color.
events.on_action: Fired when the user taps the button of a string `action`.
events.on_delete: Fired when the user taps the delete button. The chip shows the button only when this handler is set; remove the chip yourself in the handler.
events.on_text_change: Fired as the user types in an `editable` dropdown; `event.data` is the text; with 0.0.23, text such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42.
events.on_secondary_tap_down: Fired when a secondary (right) button presses down; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point.

aboutdialog.controls: Extra controls shown below the app name and version.
aboutdialog.modal: When true, tapping outside the dialog does not close it (default false). The licenses page has no backdrop, so it ignores it.
aboutdialog.barrier_color: Color of the dimmed backdrop behind the dialog. The licenses page has none.
aboutdialog.on_dismiss: Fired when the dialog or the licenses page closes, whether the user closed it or your code did; its `open` is `false` again.

actionsheet.title: Title at the top of the sheet, as a string or a control.
actionsheet.actions: The `action_sheet_action` buttons, from top to bottom.
actionsheet.cancel: An `action_sheet_action` set apart below the other actions, for closing the sheet without choosing one. On iOS and macOS it is drawn as a separate rounded button; Android, web, Windows and Linux draw it under a divider.

actionsheetaction.content: Label of the action, as a string or a control; required.
actionsheetaction.default: Draws the action in bold as the default choice.
actionsheetaction.destructive: Draws the action in red for choices such as Delete (the theme's error color on Android, web, Windows and Linux).
actionsheetaction.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown while the pointer is over the action on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
actionsheetaction.on_click: Fired when the user taps the action. The sheet does not close by itself: close it in the handler, for example with `page.close_bottom_sheet`.

alertdialog.title: Title of the dialog, as a string or a control.
alertdialog.content: Body of the dialog, usually a `text` or a `column`.
alertdialog.actions: Buttons along the bottom of the dialog. On iOS and macOS each button is drawn as an iOS dialog action; give a button `default: true` or `destructive: true` to style it.
alertdialog.modal: When true, tapping outside the dialog does not close it (default false).
alertdialog.barrier_color: Color of the dimmed backdrop behind the dialog.
alertdialog.inset_animation: How the dialog moves when the on-screen keyboard changes the space it has: `{ duration: 100, curve: "decelerate" }` (the default) or a number of milliseconds. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
alertdialog.on_dismiss: Fired when the dialog closes, whether the user tapped outside it or your code closed it; its `open` is `false` again.
alertdialog.bgcolor: Background color of the dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.icon: Icon shown above the title, as an icon name or a control. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.icon_color: Color of `icon`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.icon_padding: Padding around `icon`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.title_padding: Padding around the title. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.title_text_style: Text style of a string title, for example `{ size: 20, weight: "bold" }`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.content_padding: Padding around the content (default 24 at the sides and bottom, 20 at the top). iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.content_text_style: Default text style of the content. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.actions_padding: Padding around the row of actions. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.actions_alignment: How the actions are spread along their row: `"end"` (default), `"start"`, `"center"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.action_button_padding: Padding around each action button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.actions_overflow_button_spacing: Space between the actions when they do not fit in one row and stack vertically, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.inset_padding: Space between the dialog and the screen edges (default 40 at the sides, 24 at the top and bottom). iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.alignment: Where the dialog sits on the screen, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1.0 to 1.0, for example `{ x: 0, y: -1 }` for the top; centered by default. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.clip_behavior: How the dialog clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.elevation: Shadow depth of the dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.shadow_color: Color of the dialog's shadow. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.shape: Shape of the dialog, for example its corner radius. iOS and macOS ignore it.
alertdialog.scrollable: Lets the title and content scroll when they do not fit on the screen (default false). iOS and macOS ignore it; the iOS dialog scrolls its content by itself.
alertdialog.semantics_label: What screen readers announce when the dialog opens. iOS and macOS ignore it.

autocomplete.on_select: Fired when the user picks a suggestion. `event.data` is `{ index: 0, selection: { key: ..., value: ... } }`, with Symbol keys, so read `event.data[:index]`; `event.value` is the suggestion's value and `event.selection` its `"key"` and `"value"`, with String keys.
autocomplete.value: Text in the field; the client keeps it up to date as the user types. On iOS and macOS, in a browser too, only the starting text: a later `page.update` of `value` does not change the field there.
autocomplete.suggestions: The `auto_complete_suggestion` entries the user can pick from; the first positional argument sets them.
autocomplete.on_change: Fired as the user types; `event.data` is the text; with 0.0.23, text such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42.

autocompletesuggestion.key: Text the user's typing is matched against, ignoring case; defaults to `value`. iOS and macOS also put it in the field after a pick, in a browser too.
autocompletesuggestion.value: Text shown in the suggestion list; defaults to `key`. Android, Windows and Linux put it in the field after a pick, in a browser too.

autofillgroup.content: The control holding the fields, for example a `column` of `text_field`s with `autofill_hints`; the first positional argument sets it.

banner.actions: Buttons shown with the message. At least one is required: without one the client shows an error box instead of the banner. On iOS and macOS each action is drawn inside an iOS button that fires the action's `on_click`.
banner.bgcolor: Background color of the banner. On iOS and macOS the default is the system's secondary background color.
banner.content_padding: Padding around the message and the actions. On iOS and macOS the default is 16 on every side.
banner.force_actions_below: Puts the actions under the message instead of beside it (default false). On iOS and macOS the actions are always below the message.
banner.content_text_style: Text style of the message. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.divider_color: Color of the line under the banner. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.elevation: Shadow depth of the banner. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.leading_padding: Padding around `leading`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.min_action_bar_height: Minimum height of the row of actions, in logical pixels (default 52). iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.shadow_color: Color of the banner's shadow. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.surface_tint_color: Tint the banner's surface takes to show its elevation. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.margin: Space around the banner. iOS and macOS ignore it.
banner.on_dismiss: Fired when the banner closes; its `open` is `false` again.

barchart.group_alignment: How the bar groups are spread along the x axis, for example `"spaceEvenly"` or `"center"`.

bottomsheet.dismissible: When false, tapping outside the sheet does not close it (default true).
bottomsheet.modal: On iOS and macOS, when true, tapping outside the sheet does not close it; `dismissible` wins when both are set. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it, so use `dismissible: false` to keep the sheet open everywhere.
bottomsheet.content: The control shown in the sheet; required (the first positional argument).
bottomsheet.bgcolor: Background color of the sheet. On iOS and macOS the default is the system background color.
bottomsheet.barrier_color: Color of the dimmed backdrop behind the sheet. A `fullscreen` sheet on iOS and macOS has none.
bottomsheet.draggable: Lets the user drag the sheet down to close it (default false). On iOS and macOS a `fullscreen` sheet can be dragged unless you pass `false`.
bottomsheet.use_safe_area: Keeps the sheet's content clear of system areas such as the status bar, notches and the home indicator (default true).
bottomsheet.scrollable: Lets the sheet grow past its usual limit of 9/16 of the screen height, up to the status bar, for tall or scrolling content (default false).
bottomsheet.fullscreen: Opens the sheet at the full screen height (default false). On iOS and macOS it is shown as a stacked page sheet.
bottomsheet.maintain_bottom_view_insets_padding: Moves the content up by the height of the on-screen keyboard, so a text field in the sheet stays visible (default true).
bottomsheet.size_constraints: Size limits of the sheet, for example `{ max_width: 640 }`. A `fullscreen` sheet ignores them.
bottomsheet.padding: Padding around the content on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
bottomsheet.height: Height of the sheet on iOS and macOS; a `picker`, `timer_picker` or `date_picker` panel is 220 high by default. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
bottomsheet.on_dismiss: Fired when the sheet closes, whether the user dismissed it or your code closed it; its `open` is `false` again.
bottomsheet.elevation: Shadow depth of the sheet. iOS and macOS ignore it.
bottomsheet.shape: Shape of the sheet, for example rounded top corners. iOS and macOS ignore it.
bottomsheet.clip_behavior: How the sheet clips its content. iOS and macOS ignore it.
bottomsheet.animation_style: Durations and curves of the open and close animations: `{ duration:, reverse_duration:, curve:, reverse_curve: }`, with durations in milliseconds. iOS and macOS ignore it.

button.default: Only an alert dialog's action on iOS and macOS uses it: the action shows in bold as the default one.
button.destructive: Only an alert dialog's action on iOS and macOS uses it: the action shows in red as destructive.
button.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
button.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the button fades to while it is pressed on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
button.size: Size of the button on iOS and macOS: `"small"`, `"medium"` or `"large"` (the default). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.

checkbox.error: Shows the checkbox in its error color. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
checkbox.value: `true` when checked and `false` when not (default false); with `tristate`, `nil` for the mixed state. The client updates it when the user taps.
checkbox.label: Text or control shown next to the box; tapping it toggles the checkbox too.
checkbox.hover_color: Color of the ink circle while the pointer is over the checkbox. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
checkbox.overlay_color: Color of the ink circle when the checkbox is pressed, hovered or focused. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
checkbox.splash_radius: Radius of the ink circle, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
checkbox.visual_density: Compactness of the checkbox, for example `"compact"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
checkbox.fill_color: Color of the box; give one color or a map by state, for example `{ selected: "#16a34a" }`.
checkbox.on_change: Fired when the user toggles the checkbox. Read the new state from `event.control.props["value"]`: `event.data` is `true`, or `nil` when the box was cleared (the client sends `false`).
checkbox.active_color: Color of the box while it is checked.

chip.label: Text or control shown in the chip (required); the first positional argument sets it.
chip.selected: Whether the chip is selected (default false). With an `on_select` handler the client toggles it on each tap.
chip.leading: Control shown before the label, such as `icon("star")` or an avatar. A bare icon name such as `"star"` draws nothing.
chip.selected_color: Background color while the chip is selected.
chip.bgcolor: Background color while the chip is not selected.
chip.padding: Space inside the chip around its content.
chip.border_side: Outline of the chip, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.check_color: Color of the check mark. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.clip_behavior: How the chip clips its content: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.color: Fill color of the chip by state, for example `{ selected: "#dbeafe", default: "#f3f4f6" }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.disabled_color: Background color while the chip is disabled. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.elevation: Shadow depth of the chip. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.label_padding: Space around the label. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.label_text_style: Style of the label text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the chip, for example `"click"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.shadow_color: Color of the chip's shadow. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.shape: Shape of the chip. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.visual_density: Compactness of the chip, for example `"compact"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
chip.on_click: Fired when the user taps the chip. A chip may have `on_click` or `on_select`, not both: with both the client draws an error box.
chip.on_select: Fired when the user taps a chip that has this handler; the client toggles `selected` first. Read the new state from `event.control.props["selected"]`: `event.data` is `true`, or `nil` when the chip was deselected.

cupertinoactionsheet.title: Title at the top of the sheet, as a string or a control.
cupertinoactionsheet.actions: The `action_sheet_action` buttons, from top to bottom.
cupertinoactionsheet.cancel: An `action_sheet_action` set apart below the other actions, for closing the sheet without choosing one. On iOS and macOS it is drawn as a separate rounded button; Android, web, Windows and Linux draw it under a divider.

cupertinoactionsheetaction.content: Label of the action, as a string or a control; required.
cupertinoactionsheetaction.default: Draws the action in bold as the default choice.
cupertinoactionsheetaction.destructive: Draws the action in red for choices such as Delete (the theme's error color on Android, web, Windows and Linux).
cupertinoactionsheetaction.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown while the pointer is over the action on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoactionsheetaction.on_click: Fired when the user taps the action. The sheet does not close by itself: close it in the handler, for example with `page.close_bottom_sheet`.

cupertinoactivityindicator.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoactivityindicator.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoactivityindicator.progress: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0, the iOS name for `value`; when both are set, `progress` wins.

cupertinoalertdialog.title: Title of the dialog, as a string or a control.
cupertinoalertdialog.content: Body of the dialog, usually a `text` or a `column`.
cupertinoalertdialog.actions: Buttons along the bottom of the dialog. On iOS and macOS each button is drawn as an iOS dialog action; give a button `default: true` or `destructive: true` to style it.
cupertinoalertdialog.modal: When true, tapping outside the dialog does not close it (default false).
cupertinoalertdialog.barrier_color: Color of the dimmed backdrop behind the dialog.
cupertinoalertdialog.inset_animation: How the dialog moves when the on-screen keyboard changes the space it has: `{ duration: 100, curve: "decelerate" }` (the default) or a number of milliseconds. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoalertdialog.on_dismiss: Fired when the dialog closes, whether the user tapped outside it or your code closed it; its `open` is `false` again.

cupertinobottomsheet.dismissible: When false, tapping outside the sheet does not close it (default true).
cupertinobottomsheet.modal: On iOS and macOS, when true, tapping outside the sheet does not close it; `dismissible` wins when both are set. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it. To keep a sheet open on every platform, build it with `bottom_sheet(..., dismissible: false)`: both helpers send the same `BottomSheet` control.
cupertinobottomsheet.content: The control shown in the sheet; required (the first positional argument).
cupertinobottomsheet.bgcolor: Background color of the sheet. On iOS and macOS the default is the system background color.
cupertinobottomsheet.barrier_color: Color of the dimmed backdrop behind the sheet. A `fullscreen` sheet on iOS and macOS has none.
cupertinobottomsheet.draggable: Lets the user drag the sheet down to close it (default false). On iOS and macOS a `fullscreen` sheet can be dragged unless you pass `false`.
cupertinobottomsheet.use_safe_area: Keeps the sheet's content clear of system areas such as the status bar, notches and the home indicator (default true).
cupertinobottomsheet.scrollable: Lets the sheet grow past its usual limit of 9/16 of the screen height, up to the status bar, for tall or scrolling content (default false).
cupertinobottomsheet.fullscreen: Opens the sheet at the full screen height (default false). On iOS and macOS it is shown as a stacked page sheet.
cupertinobottomsheet.maintain_bottom_view_insets_padding: Moves the content up by the height of the on-screen keyboard, so a text field in the sheet stays visible (default true).
cupertinobottomsheet.size_constraints: Size limits of the sheet, for example `{ max_width: 640 }`. A `fullscreen` sheet ignores them.
cupertinobottomsheet.padding: Padding around the content on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinobottomsheet.height: Height of the sheet on iOS and macOS; a `picker`, `timer_picker` or `date_picker` panel is 220 high by default. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinobottomsheet.on_dismiss: Fired when the sheet closes, whether the user dismissed it or your code closed it; its `open` is `false` again.

cupertinocheckbox.value: `true` when checked and `false` when not (default false); with `tristate`, `nil` for the mixed state. The client updates it when the user taps.
cupertinocheckbox.label: Text or control shown next to the box; tapping it toggles the checkbox too.
cupertinocheckbox.fill_color: Color of the box; give one color or a map by state, for example `{ selected: "#16a34a" }`.
cupertinocheckbox.on_change: Fired when the user toggles the checkbox. Read the new state from `event.control.props["value"]`: `event.data` is `true`, or `nil` when the box was cleared (the client sends `false`).
cupertinocheckbox.active_color: Color of the box while it is checked.

cupertinodatepicker.inline: Draws the picker where you add it; this helper sends `true`. With `false` it is a dialog that `page.show_dialog` opens.
cupertinodatepicker.value: The date and time the wheels start at, for example `"2026-01-15"` or `"2026-01-15T09:30"`; after a change, the picked moment as a UTC ISO 8601 string.
cupertinodatepicker.date_picker_mode: Which wheels show: `"date"`, `"time"`, `"dateAndTime"` or `"monthYear"`. This helper sends `"date_and_time"`, which the 0.0.23 client does not recognize: it shows the date wheels only, so pass `"dateAndTime"` for a date and a time. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinodatepicker.item_extent: Height of each row of the wheels, in logical pixels (default 32). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinodatepicker.minute_interval: Step between the minutes the wheel offers, for example 5 (default 1). Use a number that divides 60. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinodatepicker.bgcolor: Background color of the wheels. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinodatepicker.first_date: Earliest moment the wheels can reach.
cupertinodatepicker.last_date: Latest moment the wheels can reach.
cupertinodatepicker.locale: Locale for month and day names, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`.
cupertinodatepicker.on_change: Fired with each change of the wheels, or, when the picker is a dialog, once the user confirms; `event.data` is the picked moment as a UTC ISO 8601 string.

cupertinopicker.controls: One control per row of the wheel, usually `text`s; the first positional argument sets them.
cupertinopicker.selected_index: Index of the row the wheel starts at (default 0); the client updates it as the user scrolls.
cupertinopicker.item_extent: Height of each row, in logical pixels (default 32). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinopicker.bgcolor: Background color of the wheel. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinopicker.on_change: Fired when the wheel settles on another row; `event.data` is the row's index.

cupertinoradio.value: The value the enclosing `radio_group` reports when the user picks this radio.
cupertinoradio.label: Text or control shown next to the radio; tapping it picks the radio too.
cupertinoradio.inactive_color: Color of the radio while it is not selected. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoradio.use_checkmark_style: Draws the selected radio as a check mark, as in iOS settings lists, instead of a filled circle (default false). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoradio.fill_color: Color of the radio's inner circle.
cupertinoradio.active_color: Color of the radio while it is selected.

cupertinosegmentedbutton.controls: One control per segment, at least two visible; the first positional argument sets them.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.selected_index: Index of the selected segment (default 0); the client updates it when the user picks another.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.border_color: Color of the border and of the lines between segments. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.selected_color: Background color of the selected segment. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.disabled_color: Background color of a disabled segment. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.padding: On iOS and macOS, space around the segments. On Android, Windows and Linux it makes the button fill the available width, inset by this padding. A browser counts as the device it runs on.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.on_change: Fired when the user picks a segment; `event.data` is its index.
cupertinosegmentedbutton.disabled_text_color: Color of the text of a disabled segment. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.

cupertinoslider.value: Current value, between `min` and `max` (the helper sends 0.0 to 1.0 by default); the client updates it while the user drags.
cupertinoslider.active_color: Color of the track up to the thumb.
cupertinoslider.on_change: Fired while the user drags. Read the value from `event.control.props["value"]`: iOS and macOS send the event without data, in a browser too.
cupertinoslider.on_change_start: Fired when the user starts dragging; `event.data` is the value.
cupertinoslider.on_change_end: Fired when the user lets go; `event.data` is the final value.

cupertinolisttile.title: Main text of the row, as a string or a control; required.
cupertinolisttile.subtitle: Secondary text below the title, as a string or a control.
cupertinolisttile.url: Opens this URL in the browser when the row is tapped.
cupertinolisttile.chevron: Adds a chevron after `trailing` to show that the row opens something (default false).
cupertinolisttile.toggle_inputs: Makes a tap anywhere on the row toggle the `switch`, `checkbox` or `radio` inside it (default false).
cupertinolisttile.padding: The `cupertino_list_tile` spelling of `content_padding`: padding inside the row.
cupertinolisttile.additional_info: Detail text shown before `trailing`, like the value on the right of an iOS Settings row, as a string or a control. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinolisttile.bgcolor_activated: Background color while the row is pressed on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinolisttile.leading_size: Size of the box `leading` is drawn in on iOS and macOS (default 28, or 30 when `notched`). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinolisttile.leading_to_title: Gap between `leading` and the title on iOS and macOS (default 16, or 12 when `notched`). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinolisttile.notched: Uses the iOS inset-grouped row style, with a larger leading area (default false). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinolisttile.on_click: Fired when the user taps the row.

cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.bgcolor: Color of the track behind the segments, on iOS and macOS. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.proportional_width: On iOS and macOS, sizes each segment to its content instead of giving all segments the same width. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.thumb_color: Color of the thumb that slides to the selected segment, on iOS and macOS. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.controls: One control per segment, at least two visible; the first positional argument sets them.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.selected_index: Index of the selected segment (default 0); the client updates it when the user picks another.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.on_change: Fired when the user picks a segment; `event.data` is its index.

cupertinoswitch.value: `true` when the switch is on (default false). The client updates it when the user toggles the switch.
cupertinoswitch.label: Text or control shown next to the switch; tapping it toggles the switch too.
cupertinoswitch.on_label_color: Color of the on mark (a line) that iOS draws in the track when the user has turned on On/Off Labels in the accessibility settings. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoswitch.off_label_color: Color of the off mark (a circle) that iOS draws in the track when the user has turned on On/Off Labels in the accessibility settings. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinoswitch.thumb_color: Color of the thumb; give one color or a map by state, for example `{ selected: "#ffffff" }`.
cupertinoswitch.on_change: Fired when the user toggles the switch. Read the new state from `event.control.props["value"]`, which the client sets first.

cupertinotextfield.value: The text in the field; the first positional argument sets it. The client updates it as the user types.
cupertinotextfield.label: Label of the field on Android, Windows and Linux. On iOS and macOS it does not show, because this helper sends an empty `placeholder_text`: use `hint_text`, which every platform shows. A browser counts as the device it runs on.
cupertinotextfield.align_label_with_hint: Aligns the label with the hint text; useful for multiline fields. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.always_call_on_tap: Fires `on_click` on every tap, even when the field already has focus. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.can_request_focus: Whether the field can take keyboard focus (default true). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.collapsed: Removes the field's decoration and padding for a minimal input. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.counter: Text or control shown below the field on the right, often a character count. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.focus_color: Highlight color of the field while it has focus. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.helper: Helper text or control shown below the field. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.helper_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of helper text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.hint_fade_duration: Time the hint takes to fade when the user starts typing, in milliseconds. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.hint_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of hint text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
