cupertinotextfield.hover_color: Highlight color of the field while the pointer is over it. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.icon: Icon shown before the field, outside its border. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.ignore_pointers: Lets taps and clicks pass through the field to what is behind it, so the user cannot focus it by tapping. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the field, for example `"text"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.size_constraints: Size limits of the field's decoration, for example `{ max_height: 40 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.prefix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits of the prefix icon, for example `{ max_width: 24 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.suffix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits of the suffix icon, for example `{ max_width: 24 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.clear_button_semantics_label: What screen readers announce for the clear button (`cupertino_text_field` sends "Clear"). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.clear_button_visibility_mode: When the clear button shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`. `cupertino_text_field` sends `"never"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.prefix_visibility_mode: When the prefix shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.suffix_visibility_mode: When the suffix shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.placeholder_text: Prompt shown while the field is empty; `hint_text` wins when both are set. Prefer `hint_text`, which every platform shows. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.padding: Space between the field's border and its text: a number for every side, or a `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }` map; this helper sends `{ all: 7 }`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too. [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the `all:` shorthand Ruflet main adds.
cupertinotextfield.blend_mode: How the field's background color or gradient is combined with what is behind it, for example `"multiply"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.gradient: Gradient that fills the field's background. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.image: Image painted behind the text, for example `{ src: "assets/paper.png", fit: "cover", opacity: 0.3 }`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.shadows: Drop shadows painted behind the field. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotextfield.on_change: Fired as the user types; `event.data` is the text, which the client also writes to `value`; with 0.0.23, text such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42.
cupertinotextfield.on_submit: Fired when the user submits the field, for example with the keyboard's done key; `event.data` is the text; with 0.0.23, text such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42. With `shift_enter`, Enter sends it without data: read `event.control.props["value"]`.
cupertinotextfield.on_selection_change: Fired when the user moves the cursor or changes the selection. `event.data` has Symbol keys: `event.data[:selected_text]` is the selected text and `event.data[:selection]` its range, with `:base_offset`, `:extent_offset`, `:affinity` and `:directional`. While this handler is set, the client also writes the range to `selection`.
cupertinotextfield.on_click: Fired when the user taps the field.
cupertinotextfield.on_tap_outside: Fired when the user taps outside the field while it has focus.
cupertinotextfield.content_padding: Space between the field's border and its text; on iOS and macOS, in a browser too, it wins over `padding`.
cupertinotextfield.fill_color: Background color of the field when `filled` is true.
cupertinotextfield.text_style: Style of the typed text, for example `{ size: 16, color: "#111827" }`.
cupertinotextfield.selection: The selected range of `value`, for example `{ base_offset: 0, extent_offset: 5 }`; set it to select text or move the cursor. While the field has an `on_selection_change` handler, the client updates it.

cupertinotimerpicker.value: The duration, in whole seconds, for example `90` for 1 min 30 s (default 0); the client updates it as the user changes it.
cupertinotimerpicker.minute_interval: Step between the minutes the picker offers, for example 5 (default 1). Use a number that divides 60.
cupertinotimerpicker.alignment: Position of the wheels in the space the picker has, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1; `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` is the center, and this helper sends `"center"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotimerpicker.bgcolor: Background color of the wheels. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotimerpicker.item_extent: Height of each row of the wheels, in logical pixels (default 32). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
cupertinotimerpicker.on_change: Fired as the user changes the duration. When `value` is an Integer, `event.data` is the new duration in seconds; otherwise it is the duration in microseconds, and `.to_i` gives the number. `event.control.props["value"]` holds the same value in both cases.

datacell.content: The cell's control, usually a `text`; required (the first positional argument).
datacell.placeholder: Marks the content as placeholder text that the user has not filled in yet, drawn in a lighter style. In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it has no effect.
datacell.show_edit_icon: Shows a pencil icon in the cell to tell users they can edit it; handle `on_tap` to start editing. In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it has no effect.
datacell.on_tap: Fired when the user taps the cell.
datacell.on_double_tap: Fired when the user double-taps the cell.
datacell.on_long_press: Fired when the user long-presses the cell.
datacell.on_tap_down: Fired when a pointer first touches the cell. `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point (`.x`, `.y`), and `event.kind` the pointer kind, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`; `event.data` holds them as `{ k:, l: { x:, y: }, g: { x:, y: } }`. In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it is never sent.
datacell.on_tap_cancel: Fired when a tap that started on the cell is cancelled. In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it is never sent.

datacolumn.on_sort: Fired when the user taps the heading to sort; `event.data[:ci]` is the column index and `event.data[:asc]` the new direction on Android, web, Windows and Linux. On iOS and macOS `event.data[:asc]` is the table's current `sort_ascending`, so keep the direction in Ruby.
datacolumn.label: Heading text or control; required (the first positional argument).
datacolumn.numeric: Right-aligns the column, for numbers (default false). In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it has no effect.
datacolumn.heading_row_alignment: How the heading is aligned in its cell: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`. In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it has no effect.
datacolumn.tooltip: Tooltip shown on the heading. In a `data_table` on iOS and macOS it has no effect.

datacolumn2.size: Relative width of the column: `"s"` (default), `"m"` or `"l"`.
datacolumn2.label: Heading text or control; required (the first positional argument).
datacolumn2.numeric: Right-aligns the column, for numbers (default false).
datacolumn2.on_sort: Fired when the user taps the heading to sort; `event.data[:ci]` is the column index and `event.data[:asc]` the new direction.

datepicker.value: The date the picker starts at, for example `"2026-01-15"`; after a pick, the picked day as a UTC ISO 8601 timestamp.
datepicker.open: Whether the dialog is open; `page.show_dialog(picker)` sets it, and the client clears it when the dialog closes.
datepicker.date_picker_mode: View the picker starts in. Android, Windows and Linux: `"day"` (the calendar, default) or `"year"`. iOS and macOS: the wheels, `"date"` (default), `"time"`, `"dateAndTime"` or `"monthYear"`. A browser counts as the device it runs on.
datepicker.entry_mode: How the dialog starts: `"calendar"` (default), `"input"` (a text field), `"calendarOnly"` or `"inputOnly"`. The client updates it when the user switches. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
datepicker.keyboard_type: Keyboard used in the dialog's input mode, for example `"datetime"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
datepicker.locale: Locale for month and day names, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`.
datepicker.inset_padding: Space between the dialog and the screen edges. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
datepicker.current_date: Date shown as today; on iOS and macOS, in a browser too, where the wheels start when `value` is not set.
datepicker.cancel_text: Label of the button that closes the picker without a pick; iOS and macOS show "Cancel" by default, in a browser too.
datepicker.modal: When true, tapping outside the picker does not close it (default false).
datepicker.bgcolor: Background color of the wheels. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
datepicker.item_extent: Height of each row of the wheels, in logical pixels (default 32). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
datepicker.minute_interval: Step between the minutes the time wheel offers, for example 5 (default 1). Use a number that divides 60. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
datepicker.on_change: Fired when the user confirms a date; `event.data` is the picked day as a UTC ISO 8601 timestamp, which the client also writes to `value`.
datepicker.on_dismiss: Fired when the picker closes, after `on_change` when the user picked a date. `event.data` is `true` when the user closed it without picking, and `nil` otherwise (the client sends `false`).
datepicker.barrier_color: Color of the scrim drawn behind the dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.

daterangepicker.start_value: First day of the range, for example `"2026-07-01"`; after a pick, a UTC ISO 8601 timestamp.
daterangepicker.end_value: Last day of the range, for example `"2026-07-07"`; after a pick, a UTC ISO 8601 timestamp.
daterangepicker.open: Whether the picker is open; `page.show_dialog(picker)` sets it, and the client clears it when the picker closes.
daterangepicker.current_date: Date shown as today. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
daterangepicker.entry_mode: How the dialog starts: `"calendar"` (default), `"input"` (two text fields), `"calendarOnly"` or `"inputOnly"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
daterangepicker.keyboard_type: Keyboard used in the dialog's input mode, for example `"datetime"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
daterangepicker.locale: Locale for month and day names, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
daterangepicker.cancel_text: Label of the button that closes the picker without a pick; iOS and macOS show "Cancel" by default, in a browser too.
daterangepicker.modal: When true, tapping outside the picker does not close it (default false).

daterangepicker.barrier_color: Color of the scrim drawn behind the dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.

datatable.border_radius: Corner radius of the table's border. iOS and macOS ignore it.

datatable.data_row_min_height: Minimum height of a data row, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.data_row_max_height: Maximum height of a data row, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.data_text_style: Text style of the cells. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.divider_thickness: Thickness of the lines between rows, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.heading_row_height: Height of the heading row, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.heading_text_style: Text style of the headings. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.horizontal_margin: Space before the first and after the last column, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
datatable.sort_column_index: Index of the column that shows the sort arrow. iOS and macOS draw no sort arrow.

datatable2.min_width: Minimum width of the table, in logical pixels; on a narrower screen the table scrolls sideways.
datatable2.show_checkbox_column: Adds a column of checkboxes for selecting rows; it shows only when at least one row has `on_select_change` (default false).
datatable2.data_row_color: Background color of the data rows.
datatable2.heading_row_color: Background color of the heading row.

draggable.on_drag_start: Fired when the user starts dragging the control.

dropdown.helper_style: Style of `helper_text`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.

dropdown.hint_style: Style of `hint_text`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
dropdown.hover_color: Background color of the field while the pointer is over it. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.

dropdown.label_style: Style of `label`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.

popupmenubutton.on_select: Fired when an item is chosen; the data is the item's internal id, so handle each item's `on_click` instead.

progressbar.value: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0; leave it unset for an indeterminate bar.
progressbar.bgcolor: Color of the track behind the filled part. On iOS and macOS the default is the system's light gray.
progressbar.color: Color of the filled part. On iOS and macOS the default is the system blue.
progressbar.track_gap: Gap between the filled part and the track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressbar.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design (the default); set `false` for the newer look with a track gap and an end dot. iOS and macOS ignore it.

progressring.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.stroke_cap: Shape of the ring's line ends: `"butt"`, `"round"` or `"square"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the ring's track, in logical pixels. It shows only with `year_2023: false`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.
progressring.value: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0; leave it unset for a spinning indicator.
progressring.progress: Progress from 0.0 to 1.0, the iOS name for `value`; when both are set, `progress` wins.
progressring.bgcolor: Color of the ring's track. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.stroke_width: Thickness of the ring, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.stroke_align: Where the stroke sits on the ring's path: `-1.0` inside, `0.0` centered, `1.0` outside (default: centered, or inside with `year_2023: false`). iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.size_constraints: Size limits of the ring, for example `{ min_width: 48, min_height: 48 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it; size the iOS indicator with `radius`.
progressring.padding: Space around the ring. iOS and macOS ignore it.

radio.value: The value the enclosing `radio_group` reports when the user picks this radio.
radio.label: Text or control shown next to the radio; tapping it picks the radio too.
radio.hover_color: Color of the ink circle while the pointer is over the radio. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
radio.overlay_color: Color of the ink circle when the radio is pressed, hovered or focused. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
radio.splash_radius: Radius of the ink circle, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
radio.visual_density: Compactness of the radio, for example `"compact"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
radio.inactive_color: Color of the radio while it is not selected. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
radio.use_checkmark_style: Draws the selected radio as a check mark, as in iOS settings lists, instead of a filled circle (default false). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
radio.fill_color: Color of the radio's fill; on Android, Windows and Linux, in a browser too, also a map by state, such as `{ selected: "#16a34a" }`.
radio.active_color: Color of the radio while it is selected.

radiogroup.value: Value of the selected radio, or `nil` for none; the client updates it when the user picks a radio.
radiogroup.content: The control holding the radios, for example a `column`; the first positional argument sets it.
radiogroup.on_change: Fired when the user picks a radio; `event.data` is that radio's `value`, which the client also writes to the group's `value`.

rangeslider.start_value: Value of the first thumb, between `min` and `end_value`; the client updates it while the user drags.
rangeslider.end_value: Value of the second thumb, between `start_value` and `max`; the client updates it while the user drags.
rangeslider.label: Text shown above a thumb while the user drags it; `{value}` is replaced by the thumb's value. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
rangeslider.round: Number of decimal places of the value in `label`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
rangeslider.inactive_color: Color of the track outside the range. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
rangeslider.overlay_color: Color of the circle drawn around a thumb while it is dragged, hovered or focused. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
rangeslider.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the slider, for example `"click"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
rangeslider.active_color: Color of the track between the thumbs.
rangeslider.on_change: Fired while the user drags a thumb, without data: read `event.control.props["start_value"]` and `["end_value"]`.
rangeslider.on_change_start: Fired when the user starts dragging a thumb, without data.
rangeslider.on_change_end: Fired when the user lets go of a thumb, without data.

reorderablelistview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels.
reorderablelistview.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the default drag handles. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
reorderablelistview.semantic_child_count: Accepted, but no Ruflet client reads it on a reorderable list.
reorderablelistview.on_reorder_end: Fired when the user drops the item, also when it lands where it started; `event.new_index` is the drop position.
reorderablelistview.on_reorder_start: Fired when the user starts dragging an item; `event.old_index` is its index.
reorderablelistview.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` is a hash with the keys `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels`, `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates, `:direction` on user events, and `:overscroll` and `:velocity` on overscroll.

responsiverow.columns: Number of virtual columns the row is divided into (default 12); `col` spans count in these.
responsiverow.alignment: How the children of a line are spread horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
responsiverow.breakpoints: Breakpoint names and the page width, in logical pixels, from which each applies (default `{ "xs" => 0, "sm" => 576, "md" => 768, "lg" => 992, "xl" => 1200, "xxl" => 1400 }`). They are compared with the page width, not the row's.
responsiverow.vertical_alignment: How the children of a line are aligned vertically: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"` or `"stretch"`.
responsiverow.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` is a hash with the keys `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels`, `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates, `:direction` on user events, and `:overscroll` and `:velocity` on overscroll.

searchbar.shrink_wrap: Sizes the open search view to its suggestions instead of filling the available height. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.controls: The suggestions listed under the bar; the first positional argument sets them. Replace them as the query changes.
searchbar.value: The query in the bar; the client updates it as the user types.
searchbar.bar_leading: Control shown at the start of the bar, for example a search icon.
searchbar.bar_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the bar.
searchbar.bar_border_side: Outline of the bar, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.bar_elevation: Shadow depth of the bar. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.bar_shape: Shape of the bar. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.bar_size_constraints: Size limits of the bar, for example `{ max_width: 480 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.capitalization: Automatic capitalization of the typed query: `"none"`, `"words"`, `"sentences"` or `"characters"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.divider_color: Color of the line between the open view's header and its suggestions. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.full_screen: Opens the search view full screen (default false). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.keyboard_type: On-screen keyboard used for the query, for example `"text"` or `"url"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.view_elevation: Shadow depth of the open search view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.view_leading: Control shown at the start of the open view's header; by default a back button. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.view_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the open view's header; by default a clear button. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.view_shape: Shape of the open search view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.view_side: Outline of the open search view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.view_size_constraints: Size limits of the open search view. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
searchbar.on_change: Fired as the user types; `event.data` is the query; with 0.0.23, a query such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42.
searchbar.on_submit: Fired when the user submits the query with the keyboard; `event.data` is the query; with 0.0.23, a query such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42.
searchbar.on_tap: Fired when the user taps the bar. To open the search view, call `open_view` here.

segment.value: Value the segmented button reports in `selected` and `on_change` (required); the first positional argument sets it.
segment.label: Text or control shown in the segment.
segment.icon: Icon or control shown in the segment.

segmentedbutton.segments: The `segment(...)` options; the first positional argument sets them.
segmentedbutton.selected: Values of the selected segments, for example `["week"]`; the client updates it when the user picks segments.
segmentedbutton.style: Button style of the segments: colors, padding and shape. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.border_color: Color of the border and of the lines between segments. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.click_color: Color of a segment while it is pressed. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.disabled_color: Background color of a disabled segment. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.selected_color: Background color of the selected segments. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.unselected_color: Background color of the segments that are not selected. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.bgcolor: With `sliding: true`, on iOS and macOS (in a browser too), color of the track behind the segments. The other designs ignore it.
segmentedbutton.thumb_color: With `sliding: true`, on iOS and macOS (in a browser too), color of the thumb that slides to the selected segment. The other designs ignore it.
segmentedbutton.proportional_width: With `sliding: true`, on iOS and macOS (in a browser too), sizes each segment to its content instead of giving all the same width. The other designs ignore it.
segmentedbutton.on_change: Fired when the user changes the selection; `event.data` is the list of selected values, which the client also writes to `selected`.
segmentedbutton.disabled_text_color: Color of the text of a disabled segment. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
segmentedbutton.show_selected_icon: Shows `selected_icon` on selected segments in place of their own icon (default true). Set `false` to keep each segment's icon; set it when you build the button, because with 0.0.23 `page.update` of this key raises ArgumentError.
segmentedbutton.selected_icon: Icon or control shown on selected segments. When it is not set, Android, Windows and Linux show a check mark there and iOS and macOS show no icon. A browser counts as the device it runs on.

semantics.header: Marks the content as a heading for screen readers.
semantics.expanded: Tells screen readers whether the content is expanded.
semantics.on_tap_hint_text: What screen readers say the tap action does, for example "Open".
semantics.on_long_press_hint_text: What screen readers say the long-press action does.
semantics.hint_text: What screen readers say acting on the control does, for example "Opens the message".
semantics.focus: Tells screen readers whether the control has input focus.
semantics.textfield: Tells screen readers that the content is a text field.
semantics.identifier: An identifier for UI tests and platform accessibility tools; screen readers do not announce it.
semantics.button: Tells screen readers the content is a button.
semantics.container: Makes the content its own element for screen readers instead of merging it into the parent (default `false`).
semantics.content: The control described to screen readers; the first positional argument sets it.
semantics.current_value_length: Number of characters entered so far, for a text field.
semantics.decreased_value: Value screen readers announce after `on_decrease`, such as `"40%"`.
semantics.exclude_semantics: Hides the content's own semantics, so screen readers announce only what this control says (default `false`).
semantics.focusable: Tells screen readers the content can take input focus.
semantics.heading_level: Heading level from 1 to 6, used with `header: true`.
semantics.hidden: Tells screen readers the content is hidden, such as an inactive page.
semantics.image: Tells screen readers the content is an image.
semantics.increased_value: Value screen readers announce after `on_increase`, such as `"60%"`.
semantics.label: Text screen readers announce for the content.
semantics.link: Tells screen readers the content is a link.
semantics.live_region: Announces changes to the label as they happen, as for a status message.
semantics.max_value_length: Largest number of characters allowed, for a text field.
semantics.mixed: Tells screen readers a checkbox is in a mixed (partly checked) state.
semantics.multiline: Tells screen readers a text field takes more than one line.
semantics.obscured: Tells screen readers a text field hides its text, as for a password.
semantics.read_only: Tells screen readers a text field cannot be edited.
semantics.selected: Tells screen readers the content is selected.
semantics.checked: Tells screen readers a checkbox or switch is checked.
semantics.slider: Tells screen readers the content is a slider.
semantics.toggled: Tells screen readers a switch is on.
semantics.value: Current value screen readers announce, such as `"50%"` for a slider. It does not change what is displayed.
semantics.on_copy: Fired when a screen reader asks to copy.
semantics.on_cut: Fired when a screen reader asks to cut.
semantics.on_decrease: Fired when a screen reader asks to decrease the value, for example with a swipe down on a slider.
semantics.on_did_gain_accessibility_focus: Fired when the screen reader's focus moves onto the content.
semantics.on_did_lose_accessibility_focus: Fired when the screen reader's focus leaves the content.
semantics.on_dismiss: Fired when a screen reader asks to dismiss the content.
semantics.on_increase: Fired when a screen reader asks to increase the value, for example with a swipe up on a slider.
semantics.on_move_cursor_backward_by_character: Fired when a screen reader moves the text cursor back one character; `event.data` is true when it extends the selection.
semantics.on_move_cursor_forward_by_character: Fired when a screen reader moves the text cursor forward one character; `event.data` is true when it extends the selection.
semantics.on_paste: Fired when a screen reader asks to paste.
semantics.on_scroll_down: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll down.
semantics.on_scroll_left: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll left.
semantics.on_scroll_right: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll right.
semantics.on_scroll_up: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll up.
semantics.on_set_text: Fired when a screen reader sets a text field's text; `event.data` is the new text.
semantics.on_tap: Fired when a screen reader activates the content, for example with a double tap in VoiceOver or TalkBack.
semantics.on_double_tap: Fired when the user double-taps the content.
semantics.on_long_press: Fired when a screen reader performs a long press on the content.

shimmer.base_color: Color of the content between highlights. Give it with `highlight_color`, or use `gradient` instead.
shimmer.content: The placeholder controls the shimmer sweeps over, usually grey boxes; the first positional argument sets it.
shimmer.gradient: Gradient swept over the content instead of `base_color` and `highlight_color`: `{ _type: "linear", colors: [...] }`.
shimmer.loop: Number of sweeps before the shimmer stops; `0` (default) loops forever.
shimmer.period: Time one sweep takes, in milliseconds (default 1500).

slider.value: Current value, between `min` and `max` (default 0.0 to 1.0); the client updates it while the user drags.
slider.label: Text shown above the thumb while the user drags it; `{value}` is replaced by the value. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.round: Number of decimal places of the value in `label` (default 0). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.inactive_color: Color of the track after the thumb. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.overlay_color: Color of the circle drawn around the thumb while it is dragged, hovered or focused. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the slider, for example `"click"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.padding: Space around the track. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.year_2023: With `false`, draws the newer Material 3 slider instead of the 2023 design. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
slider.active_color: Color of the track up to the thumb.
slider.on_change: Fired while the user drags. Read the value from `event.control.props["value"]`: iOS and macOS send the event without data, in a browser too, and other platforms send the value.
slider.on_change_start: Fired when the user starts dragging; `event.data` is the value.
slider.on_change_end: Fired when the user lets go; `event.data` is the final value.

snackbar.action: The action button: a string label, whose button fires the snack bar's `on_action`, or a `snack_bar_action`, whose own `on_click` fires.
snackbar.duration: How long the snack bar stays visible, in milliseconds (default 4000).
snackbar.content: The message, usually a `text`; required (the first positional argument).
snackbar.persist: Keeps the snack bar open after `duration` until the user taps its action or close icon. On Android, web, Windows and Linux a snack bar with an `action` persists unless you pass `false`; on iOS and macOS it closes after `duration` unless you pass `true`.
snackbar.show_close_icon: Shows a close (x) button that dismisses the snack bar.
snackbar.bgcolor: Background color. On iOS and macOS the default is the system gray.
snackbar.padding: Padding inside the snack bar. On iOS and macOS the default is 16 on the left, 8 on the right and 10 above and below.
snackbar.margin: Space around a `"floating"` snack bar; ignored when `width` is set. On iOS and macOS it is the space around the bar (default 12 at the sides and bottom).
snackbar.width: Width of a `"floating"` snack bar. On iOS and macOS it sets the bar's width.
snackbar.behavior: `"fixed"` (default) spans the bottom edge of the screen; `"floating"` floats above it, and only then are `margin` and `width` used. iOS and macOS ignore it: their snack bar always floats near the bottom.
snackbar.action_overflow_threshold: Fraction of the snack bar's width, from 0.0 to 1.0, that the action may take before it moves below the message (default 0.25). iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.dismiss_direction: Which swipes dismiss the snack bar, for example `"down"` (the default) or `"horizontal"`. iOS and macOS ignore it: the bar cannot be swiped away there.
snackbar.close_icon_color: Color of the close button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.clip_behavior: How the snack bar clips its content (default `"hardEdge"`). iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.elevation: Shadow depth of the snack bar. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.shape: Shape of the snack bar. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbar.on_visible: Fired when the snack bar appears.
snackbar.on_dismiss: Fired when the snack bar closes on its own: its time ran out, or the user swiped it away or tapped its action or close icon. Its `open` is `false` again.

snackbaraction.label: Text of the button; required (the first positional argument).
snackbaraction.text_color: Color of the label. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.bgcolor: Background color of the button. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled_text_color: Color of the label once the button has been pressed: an action works only once. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled_bgcolor: Background color once the button has been pressed. iOS and macOS ignore it.
snackbaraction.disabled: Disables the button on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
snackbaraction.on_click: Fired when the user taps the button. On Android, web, Windows and Linux the snack bar then closes; on iOS and macOS it stays until its time runs out.

spinkit.variant: The indicator style; set it with the variant keyword you pass to `spinkit`, such as `three_bounce:`.
spinkit.size: Size of the indicator, in logical pixels (default 50).
spinkit.duration: Length of one animation cycle, in milliseconds.
spinkit.line_width: Line thickness of the `ring` and `dual_ring` variants (default 7) and of `spinning_lines` (default 2), in logical pixels.
spinkit.border_width: Border thickness of the `ripple` variant, in logical pixels (default 6).

switch.value: `true` when the switch is on (default false). The client updates it when the user toggles the switch.
switch.label: Text or control shown next to the switch; tapping it toggles the switch too.
switch.label_text_style: Style of a text `label`, for example `{ size: 14, color: "#6b7280" }`.
switch.active_color: Color of the thumb while the switch is on. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too: use `thumb_color`.
switch.hover_color: Color of the ink circle while the pointer is over the switch. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
switch.overlay_color: Color of the ink circle when the switch is pressed, hovered or focused. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
switch.splash_radius: Radius of the ink circle, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
switch.track_color: Color of the track by state, for example `{ selected: "#16a34a" }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too: use `active_track_color` and `inactive_track_color`.
switch.padding: Space around the switch. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
switch.on_label_color: Color of the on mark (a line) that iOS draws in the track when the user has turned on On/Off Labels in the accessibility settings. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
switch.off_label_color: Color of the off mark (a circle) that iOS draws in the track when the user has turned on On/Off Labels in the accessibility settings. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
switch.thumb_color: Color of the thumb; give one color or a map by state, for example `{ selected: "#ffffff" }`.
switch.on_change: Fired when the user toggles the switch. Read the new state from `event.control.props["value"]`, which the client sets first.

textfield.value: The text in the field; the first positional argument sets it. The client updates it as the user types.
textfield.label: Label of the field. On iOS and macOS, in a browser too, a text label is the placeholder instead, when `hint_text` and `placeholder_text` are not set.
textfield.align_label_with_hint: Aligns the label with the hint text; useful for multiline fields. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.always_call_on_tap: Fires `on_click` on every tap, even when the field already has focus. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.can_request_focus: Whether the field can take keyboard focus (default true). iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.collapsed: Removes the field's decoration and padding for a minimal input. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.counter: Text or control shown below the field on the right, often a character count. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.focus_color: Highlight color of the field while it has focus. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.helper: Helper text or control shown below the field. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.helper_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of helper text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.hint_fade_duration: Time the hint takes to fade when the user starts typing, in milliseconds. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.hint_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of hint text. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.hover_color: Highlight color of the field while the pointer is over it. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.icon: Icon shown before the field, outside its border. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.ignore_pointers: Lets taps and clicks pass through the field to what is behind it, so the user cannot focus it by tapping. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the field, for example `"text"`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.size_constraints: Size limits of the field's decoration, for example `{ max_height: 40 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.prefix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits of the prefix icon, for example `{ max_width: 24 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.suffix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits of the suffix icon, for example `{ max_width: 24 }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.clear_button_semantics_label: What screen readers announce for the clear button (`cupertino_text_field` sends "Clear"). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.clear_button_visibility_mode: When the clear button shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`. `cupertino_text_field` sends `"never"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.prefix_visibility_mode: When the prefix shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.suffix_visibility_mode: When the suffix shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.placeholder_text: Prompt shown while the field is empty; `hint_text` wins when both are set. Prefer `hint_text`, which every platform shows. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.padding: Space between the field's border and its text: a number for every side, or a `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }` map; `cupertino_text_field` sends `{ all: 7 }`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too. [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the `all:` shorthand Ruflet main adds.
textfield.blend_mode: How the field's background color or gradient is combined with what is behind it, for example `"multiply"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.gradient: Gradient that fills the field's background. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.image: Image painted behind the text, for example `{ src: "assets/paper.png", fit: "cover", opacity: 0.3 }`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.shadows: Drop shadows painted behind the field. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
textfield.on_change: Fired as the user types; `event.data` is the text, which the client also writes to `value`; with 0.0.23, text such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42.
textfield.on_submit: Fired when the user submits the field, for example with the keyboard's done key; `event.data` is the text; with 0.0.23, text such as `42` arrives parsed, as the Integer 42. With `shift_enter`, Enter sends it without data: read `event.control.props["value"]`.
textfield.on_selection_change: Fired when the user moves the cursor or changes the selection. `event.data` has Symbol keys: `event.data[:selected_text]` is the selected text and `event.data[:selection]` its range, with `:base_offset`, `:extent_offset`, `:affinity` and `:directional`. While this handler is set, the client also writes the range to `selection`.
textfield.on_click: Fired when the user taps the field.
textfield.on_tap_outside: Fired when the user taps outside the field while it has focus.
textfield.content_padding: Space between the field's border and its text; on iOS and macOS, in a browser too, it wins over `padding`.
textfield.fill_color: Background color of the field when `filled` is true.
textfield.text_style: Style of the typed text, for example `{ size: 16, color: "#111827" }`.
textfield.selection: The selected range of `value`, for example `{ base_offset: 0, extent_offset: 5 }`; set it to select text or move the cursor. While the field has an `on_selection_change` handler, the client updates it.

timepicker.value: The time the picker starts at, for example `"09:30"`; after a pick, the picked time as `"H:M"` without leading zeros, such as `"9:5"` for 09:05.
timepicker.open: Whether the picker is open; `page.show_dialog(picker)` sets it, and the client clears it when the picker closes.
timepicker.entry_mode: How the dialog starts: `"dial"` (default), `"input"`, `"dialOnly"` or `"inputOnly"`. The client updates it when the user switches. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
timepicker.help_text: Title shown at the top of the dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
timepicker.locale: Locale of the dialog, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.
timepicker.cancel_text: Label of the button that closes the picker without a pick; iOS and macOS show "Cancel" by default, in a browser too.
timepicker.modal: When true, tapping outside the picker does not close it (default false).
timepicker.on_change: Fired when the user confirms a time; `event.data` is the time as `"H:M"` without leading zeros, such as `"14:5"`, which the client also writes to `value`.
timepicker.on_dismiss: Fired when the picker closes, after `on_change` when the user picked a time. `event.data` is `true` when the user closed it without picking, and `nil` otherwise (the client sends `false`).
timepicker.barrier_color: Color of the scrim drawn behind the dialog. iOS and macOS ignore it, in a browser too.

timerpicker.value: The duration, in whole seconds, for example `90` for 1 min 30 s (default 0); the client updates it as the user changes it.
timerpicker.minute_interval: Step between the minutes the picker offers, for example 5 (default 1). Use a number that divides 60.
timerpicker.alignment: Position of the wheels in the space the picker has, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1; `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` is the center, and `cupertino_timer_picker` sends `"center"`. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
timerpicker.bgcolor: Background color of the wheels. Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
timerpicker.item_extent: Height of each row of the wheels, in logical pixels (default 32). Android, Windows and Linux ignore it, in a browser too.
timerpicker.on_change: Fired as the user changes the duration. When `value` is an Integer, `event.data` is the new duration in seconds; otherwise it is the duration in microseconds, and `.to_i` gives the number. `event.control.props["value"]` holds the same value in both cases.

table.rows: The `table_row` rows; the first positional argument, `rows:` or a block sets them.
table.border_color: Color of the table's lines; nothing is drawn without it.
table.border_width: Width of the lines, in logical pixels (default 1).
table.border_radius: Corner radius of the outer border.

tablerow.controls: The row's cells; the first positional argument, `controls:` or a block sets them. A hidden cell keeps its column.

absorbpointer.absorbing: When true (default), the content gets no taps or other pointer input, and neither does anything behind it. Set `false` to let the content react again.
absorbpointer.content: The control whose pointer input is blocked; the first positional argument sets it.

animatedswitcher.content: The control shown now. Replace it with `page.update(switcher, content: ...)` to animate to the new one.
animatedswitcher.duration: Length of the animation to new content, in milliseconds (default 1000).
animatedswitcher.reverse_duration: Length of the animation of the outgoing content, in milliseconds (default: `duration`).
animatedswitcher.switch_in_curve: Easing curve of the incoming content, for example `"easeOut"` (default linear).
animatedswitcher.switch_out_curve: Easing curve of the outgoing content, for example `"easeIn"` (default linear).

badge.alignment: Corner the badge sits on, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the top right, `{ x: 1, y: -1 }`).
badge.bgcolor: Color of the badge (red by default).
badge.label: Text or control shown in the badge; the first positional argument sets it. Give a String: a number is not shown as a label, so write `badge(count.to_s)`. Without a label, Android, web, Windows and Linux draw a small dot; iOS and macOS need a label.
badge.label_visible: Shows the badge (default `true`); `false` hides it without removing it.
badge.large_size: Height of a badge with a label, in logical pixels (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 18 on iOS and macOS).
badge.offset: Moves the badge from its corner, as `{ x:, y: }` in logical pixels.
badge.padding: Horizontal space between the label and the badge's edge, in logical pixels.
badge.small_size: Diameter of the dot drawn when the badge has no label, in logical pixels (default 6 on Android, web, Windows and Linux).
badge.text_color: Color of the label text (white by default).
badge.text_style: Text style of the label, as a hash such as `{ size: 10, weight: "bold" }`.

card.semantic_container: Treats the card and its content as one element for screen readers (default `true`); `false` lets screen readers visit each child on its own.
card.show_border_on_foreground: Draws the `shape` border over the content instead of behind it (default `true`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only; iOS and macOS ignore it.

carouselview.consume_max_weight: With `flex_weights`, lets items grow to the largest weight as they scroll in (default `true`); `false` keeps the layout fixed. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
carouselview.enable_splash: Shows the tap ripple or highlight on items (default `true`).
carouselview.horizontal: Scrolls the items horizontally (default `true`); `false` scrolls them vertically.
carouselview.flex_weights: A weighted layout such as `[1, 7, 1]`: the visible items share the width in these proportions. It wins over `item_extent`.
carouselview.initial_item: Index of the item shown first (default 0).
carouselview.item_clip_behavior: How each item is clipped to its rounded shape: `"antiAlias"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
carouselview.item_extent: Width of each item in logical pixels (height when `horizontal: false`). A carousel needs `item_extent` or `flex_weights`.
carouselview.item_snapping: Snaps to the nearest item when the user stops scrolling (default `false`).
carouselview.overlay_color: Color of the highlight drawn over an item while it is pressed or hovered.
carouselview.shrink_extent: Smallest size, in logical pixels, an item shrinks to as it scrolls off the edge (default 0). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
carouselview.on_item_click: Fired when the user taps an item; `event.data` is its index.

circleavatar.max_radius: Largest radius the avatar may grow to, in logical pixels.
circleavatar.min_radius: Smallest radius the avatar may shrink to, in logical pixels.
circleavatar.radius: Radius of the avatar, in logical pixels (default 20).
circleavatar.on_image_error: Fired when `foreground_image_src` or `background_image_src` fails to load; `event.data` is `"foreground"` or `"background"`.

clipoval.clip_behavior: How the edge is clipped: `"antiAlias"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
clipoval.content: The control to clip; the first positional argument sets it.

cliprsuperellipse.border_radius: Corner radius: one number for every corner, or `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }` (missing corners stay square).
cliprsuperellipse.clip_behavior: How the edge is clipped: `"antiAlias"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
cliprsuperellipse.content: The control to clip; the first positional argument sets it.

column.animate_changes: Animates children that `page.update` adds or removes, as `item_animation` says (default `false`). It has no effect with `wrap: true`.
column.alignment: How the children are spread vertically: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
column.horizontal_alignment: How the children are aligned horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"` or `"stretch"`.
column.intrinsic_width: Makes the column as wide as its widest child.
column.item_animation: How `animate_changes` animates added and removed children: `{ type:, duration:, curve: }`, where `type` is `"fade"`, `"size"`, `"fade_size"` (default) or `"slide"` and `duration` defaults to 250 milliseconds.
column.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh indicator. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
column.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
column.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull to start a refresh. iOS and macOS only.
column.run_alignment: With `wrap: true`, how the columns of children are spread horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
column.run_spacing: With `wrap: true`, space between the columns of children, in logical pixels (default 10).
column.spacing: Space between the children, in logical pixels (default 10).
column.wrap: Flows the children into a new column when they do not fit vertically, instead of overflowing.
column.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` is a hash with the keys `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels`, `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates, `:direction` on user events, and `:overscroll` and `:velocity` on overscroll.

container.alignment: Where the content sits inside the container, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1; `"center"` is also accepted. [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the other names Ruflet main adds, such as `"top_left"`.
container.animate: Animates the container's size, padding, colors, border and other decoration when they change: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
container.blur: Blurs what is behind the container (frosted glass): a sigma such as `10`, `[x, y]`, or `{ sigma_x:, sigma_y: }`.
container.border_radius: Corner radius, in logical pixels: one number, or `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }`, where a corner you leave out stays square. It also clips the content. [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the `all:` shorthand Ruflet main adds.
container.color_filter: Tints the container and its content: `{ color:, blend_mode: }`, for example `{ color: "#80000000", blend_mode: "darken" }`.
container.dark_theme: Theme for the controls inside the container while the app is in dark mode, in the same form as `page.dark_theme`.
container.ignore_interactions: Makes the container and its content ignore taps and other pointer input.
container.image: Background image painted behind the content: `{ src:, fit:, alignment:, repeat:, opacity: }`.
container.ink: Shows touch feedback on a clickable container: an ink ripple on Android, web, Windows and Linux, and a fade to `opacity_on_click` on iOS and macOS.
container.ink_color: Color of the ink ripple when `ink: true`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
container.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, a clickable container with `ink: true` fades to while it is pressed (default 0.4). iOS and macOS only.
container.padding: Space between the container's edge and its content, in logical pixels: one number, or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`, where a side you leave out is 0. [Option values](/docs/controls-and-layout#option-values) lists the `all:` shorthand Ruflet main adds.
container.shadow: Drop shadow, or a list of them: `{ color:, offset: { x:, y: }, blur_radius:, spread_radius: }`.
container.theme: Theme for the controls inside the container, in the same form as `page.theme`.
container.theme_mode: Forces the container's content into `"light"` or `"dark"` mode, or `"system"`.
container.url: URL opened when the container is tapped.
container.on_click: Fired when the container is tapped.
container.on_hover: Fired when the pointer enters or leaves the container. `event.data` is `true` on enter; on leave the client sends `false`, which arrives in Ruby as `nil`.

customscrollview.controls: The slivers, when they are given in a block; prefer `slivers`.
customscrollview.slivers: The slivers, in scroll order: `sliver_app_bar`, `sliver_list`, `sliver_grid`, `sliver_to_box_adapter`, `sliver_fill_remaining`, `sliver_padding`, or any other control, which scrolls as one box. The first positional argument sets them.
customscrollview.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` is a hash with the keys `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels`, `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates, `:direction` on user events, and `:overscroll` and `:velocity` on overscroll.

dismissible.on_dismiss: Fired when the control has been swiped away; `event.direction` is the swipe direction, such as `"startToEnd"` or `"endToStart"`. Remove the control from its parent in this handler.
dismissible.on_resize: Fired while the space left by the dismissed control closes.
dismissible.on_update: Fired while the user drags; `event.direction` is the direction, `event.progress` how far the control has moved (0.0 to 1.0) and `event.reached` whether it is past the dismiss threshold.

divider.height: Total height the divider takes, with the line in the middle (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 1 on iOS and macOS).
divider.leading_indent: Empty space before the line starts, in logical pixels (default 0).
divider.radius: Corner radius of the line's ends, in logical pixels.
divider.thickness: Thickness of the line, in logical pixels (default 0.5 on iOS and macOS).
divider.trailing_indent: Empty space after the line ends, in logical pixels (default 0).

draggablescrollablesheet.elevation: Shadow depth of the sheet. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
draggablescrollablesheet.extent_change_interval: Minimum time between two `on_extent_change` events, in milliseconds (default 50); a finished drag always reports where the sheet stopped.
draggablescrollablesheet.initial_child_size: Size of the sheet when it first shows, as a fraction of its parent's height (default 0.5).
draggablescrollablesheet.max_child_size: Largest size of the sheet, as a fraction of its parent's height (default 1.0).
draggablescrollablesheet.min_child_size: Smallest size of the sheet, as a fraction of its parent's height (default 0.25).
draggablescrollablesheet.should_close_on_min_extent: Lets dragging the sheet to its minimum size close an enclosing modal sheet (default `true`).
draggablescrollablesheet.snap_animation_duration: How long snapping to a size takes, in milliseconds.
draggablescrollablesheet.snap_sizes: Extra sizes, as fractions between `min_child_size` and `max_child_size`, that the sheet can snap to when `snap: true`.
draggablescrollablesheet.on_extent_change: Fired as the sheet size changes; `event.data` has the keys `:extent`, `:min` and `:max`, as fractions of the parent's height.

dragtarget.content: The control the user drops onto; the first positional argument sets it.
dragtarget.group: Name of the drag group this target accepts (default `"default"`). It accepts only a `draggable` with the same `group`.
dragtarget.on_accept: Fired when a draggable of the same group is dropped on the target; `event.src_id` is the draggable's id (look it up with `page.get_control(event.src_id)`) and `event.x` / `event.y` where it was dropped.
dragtarget.on_leave: Fired when a dragged control leaves the target without being dropped. The client sends the draggable's id as a two-item list, so read it from `event.data[1]`; `event.src_id` is nil here.
dragtarget.on_move: Fired as a dragged control of the same group moves over the target; `event.src_id` is its id and `event.x` / `event.y` its position.
dragtarget.on_will_accept: Fired when a dragged control enters the target; `event.accept` is true when its group matches, and `event.src_id` is its id.

fadetransition.animating: Runs the animation while true (default); `false` pauses it where it is, and `true` resumes it.
fadetransition.curve: Easing curve of each run, for example `"easeInOut"` (default linear).
fadetransition.delay: Milliseconds to wait before the first run.
fadetransition.duration: Length of one run, in milliseconds (default 1000).
fadetransition.reverse: With `repeat: true`, plays back and forth instead of restarting from `begin`.
fadetransition.on_animation_end: Fired when a run that does not repeat finishes; `event.data` is `"transition"`. An `animate_*` animation on the same control reports its own name, as on other controls.
fadetransition.begin: Opacity the animation starts from, from 0 to 1 (default 0).
fadetransition.end: Opacity the animation ends at, from 0 to 1 (default 1).
fadetransition.content: The control to fade; the first positional argument sets it.

fittedbox.alignment: Where the scaled content sits in the box, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 or a name such as `"top_left"` (default the center).
fittedbox.clip_behavior: How content that does not fit is clipped: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`.
fittedbox.content: The control to scale; the first positional argument sets it.
fittedbox.fit: How the content is scaled into the box: `"contain"` (default), `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"scaleDown"` or `"none"`.

fractionallysizedbox.alignment: Where the sized content sits in the available space, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 or a name such as `"top_left"` (default the center).
fractionallysizedbox.content: The control to size; the first positional argument sets it.
fractionallysizedbox.height_factor: Height as a fraction of the height the parent offers, such as `0.5`; leave it out to let the content choose. The parent must bound the height.
fractionallysizedbox.width_factor: Width as a fraction of the width the parent offers, such as `0.5`; leave it out to let the content choose. The parent must bound the width.

gesturedetector.on_double_tap_cancel: Fired when a possible double tap turns out not to be one.
gesturedetector.on_double_tap_down: Fired when the second tap of a double tap presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_enter: Fired when a mouse pointer enters the control; `event.local_position`, `event.global_position` and `event.kind` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_exit: Fired when a mouse pointer leaves the control; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give where.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_end: Fired when a pressure-sensitive press ends; `event.pressure` is the last pressure. Only devices with force touch send it.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_peak: Fired when a pressure-sensitive press reaches its peak; `event.pressure` gives the pressure.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_start: Fired when a pressure-sensitive press starts; `event.pressure` gives the pressure.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_update: Fired as the pressure of a press changes; `event.pressure` and `event.local_position` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_cancel: Fired when a horizontal drag is cancelled before it starts.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_down: Fired when a pointer that may start a horizontal drag presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_end: Fired when a horizontal drag ends; `event.velocity` is the speed in pixels per second and `event.primary_velocity` the horizontal part.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_start: Fired when a horizontal drag starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_update: Fired as a horizontal drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update and `event.primary_delta` its horizontal part.
gesturedetector.on_hover: Fired as a mouse pointer moves over the control, at most once per `hover_interval`; `event.local_position` gives the point and `event.local_delta` the movement.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_cancel: Fired when a press that could become a long press is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_down: Fired when a pointer that may become a long press presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_end: Fired when the finger lifts after a long press; `event.local_position` and `event.velocity` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_move_update: Fired as the finger moves during a long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_start: Fired when a long press is recognized; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_up: Fired when the finger lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_multi_long_press: Fired after `multi_tap_touches` fingers stay down for a second.
gesturedetector.on_multi_tap: Fired when several fingers touch at once; `event.correct_touches` is true when the count reached `multi_tap_touches`.
gesturedetector.on_pan_cancel: Fired when a drag is cancelled before it starts.
gesturedetector.on_pan_down: Fired when a pointer that may start a drag presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_pan_end: Fired when a drag in any direction ends; `event.velocity` is the speed in pixels per second.
gesturedetector.on_pan_start: Fired when a drag in any direction starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_pan_update: Fired as a drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update and `event.local_position` the point.
gesturedetector.on_right_pan_end: Fired when a drag with the right mouse button ends; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_right_pan_start: Fired when a drag with the right mouse button starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_right_pan_update: Fired as a right-button drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update.
gesturedetector.on_scale_end: Fired when a pinch or rotation ends; `event.velocity` and `event.pointer_count` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_scale_start: Fired when a pinch or two-finger rotation starts; `event.local_focal_point` and `event.pointer_count` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_scale_update: Fired as a pinch or rotation changes; `event.scale` is the scale since the start, `event.rotation` the rotation in radians and `event.focal_point_delta` the movement.
gesturedetector.on_scroll: Fired when the user scrolls with a mouse wheel or trackpad over the control; `event.scroll_delta` is the scroll amount and `event.local_position` the pointer.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press: Fired on a long press with the secondary (right) button.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_cancel: Fired when a secondary-button press that could become a long press is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_down: Fired when the secondary button presses down for a possible long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_end: Fired when the secondary button lifts after a long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_move_update: Fired as the pointer moves during a secondary-button long press.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_start: Fired when a secondary-button long press is recognized; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_up: Fired when the secondary button lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_tap: Fired on a secondary (right-button) click; it carries no position, so use `on_secondary_tap_down` or `on_secondary_tap_up` for the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_tap_cancel: Fired when a secondary-button tap is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_tap_up: Fired when a secondary button lifts after a tap; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tap: Fired on a tap; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point where it pressed down.
gesturedetector.on_tap_cancel: Fired when a tap is cancelled, for example because the pointer moved away.
gesturedetector.on_tap_move: Fired as the pointer moves while pressed down; `event.delta` is the movement.
gesturedetector.on_tap_up: Fired when the pointer of a tap lifts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press: Fired on a long press with the middle mouse button.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_cancel: Fired when a middle-button press that could become a long press is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_down: Fired when the middle button presses down for a possible long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_end: Fired when the middle button lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_move_update: Fired as the pointer moves during a middle-button long press.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_start: Fired when a middle-button long press is recognized.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_up: Fired when the middle button lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_tap_cancel: Fired when a middle-button tap is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_tap_down: Fired when the middle mouse button presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_tap_up: Fired when the middle mouse button lifts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_cancel: Fired when a vertical drag is cancelled before it starts.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_down: Fired when a pointer that may start a vertical drag presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_end: Fired when a vertical drag ends; `event.velocity` is the speed in pixels per second and `event.primary_velocity` the vertical part.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_start: Fired when a vertical drag starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_update: Fired as a vertical drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update and `event.primary_delta` its vertical part.

gridview.child_aspect_ratio: Width-to-height ratio of each cell (default 1, square cells).
gridview.max_extent: Largest width of a cell, in logical pixels (height for a horizontal grid); the grid fits as many columns as it can. It wins over `runs_count`.
gridview.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh indicator. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
gridview.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
gridview.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull to start a refresh. iOS and macOS only.
gridview.run_spacing: Space between the columns of cells, in logical pixels (default 10).
gridview.runs_count: Number of columns (rows for a horizontal grid), default 1.
gridview.spacing: Space between the rows of cells, in logical pixels (default 10).
gridview.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` is a hash with the keys `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels`, `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates, `:direction` on user events, and `:overscroll` and `:velocity` on overscroll.

hero.content: The control that flies to its new place; the first positional argument sets it.
hero.tag: A value, such as a String, that pairs this hero with the hero of the same tag on the next view. Every hero on one view needs its own tag.
hero.transition_on_user_gestures: Also flies the hero when the user goes back with a gesture, such as the iOS back swipe (default `false`).

icon.apply_text_scaling: Scales the icon with the user's text size setting.
icon.fill: Fill of a variable icon font such as Material Symbols, from 0 (outlined) to 1 (filled). Fonts without that axis ignore it, like `grade`, `weight` and `optical_size`.
icon.grade: Grade (stroke thickness at the same size) of a variable icon font, for example -25 to 200.
icon.icon: Icon to show: a Material icon name such as `"settings"`, or `Ruflet::Icons` and `Ruflet::CupertinoIcons` constants; the first positional argument sets it.
icon.optical_size: Optical size of a variable icon font, for example 20 to 48.
icon.size: Size of the icon, in logical pixels (default 24).
icon.weight: Stroke weight of a variable icon font, for example 100 to 700.

ignorepointer.content: The control that ignores pointer input; the first positional argument sets it.
ignorepointer.ignoring: When true (default), the content ignores taps and other pointer input, which reach whatever lies behind it. Set `false` to let the content react again.

image.anti_alias: Smooths the image's edges when it is drawn scaled or rotated (default `false`).
image.cache_height: Decodes the image at this height, in physical pixels, to save memory for large images.
image.cache_width: Decodes the image at this width, in physical pixels, to save memory for large images.
image.color: Color blended into the image with `color_blend_mode`, for example to tint an icon-like image.
image.color_blend_mode: How `color` is blended into the image, for example `"srcIn"` to tint it or `"multiply"`.
image.error_content: Control shown in place of the image when it fails to load.
image.fade_in_animation: Fades the image in once it has loaded: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
image.fit: How the image fills its box: `"contain"`, `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"scaleDown"` or `"none"`.
image.gapless_playback: Keeps showing the old image while a new `src` loads, instead of a blank space.
image.paint: How the image is drawn when it is a shape inside a `canvas`, built with `paint(...)`. An image on the page ignores it.
image.placeholder_fade_out_animation: Fades the placeholder out once the image has loaded: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration: 300, curve: "easeOut" }`.
image.placeholder_fit: How the placeholder fills the box (default: `fit`).
image.placeholder_src: Image shown while `src` loads: a URL, an asset path or Base64 data.
image.repeat: Tiles the image to fill its box: `"noRepeat"` (default), `"repeat"`, `"repeatX"` or `"repeatY"`.
image.src: The image: a URL, a path in the app's assets, Base64 data or bytes; the first positional argument sets it.
image.src_base64: The image as a Base64 string, used when `src` is not set. `src` also accepts a Base64 string, which works with every release.
image.x: Left edge of the image, in logical pixels, when it is a shape inside a `canvas`. An image on the page ignores it.
image.y: Top edge of the image, in logical pixels, when it is a shape inside a `canvas`. An image on the page ignores it.

indexedstack.alignment: Where a child smaller than the stack sits, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 or a name such as `"center"` (default the top left).
indexedstack.fit: How the shown child is sized: `"loose"` (default, its own size), `"expand"` (the stack's size) or `"passThrough"`.
indexedstack.index: Index of the one child shown, starting at 0 (default 0). Every child stays built, so each keeps its state while hidden.

interactiveviewer.alignment: Accepted, but current clients cannot apply it: a viewer with `alignment` set fails to build. Leave it out.
interactiveviewer.boundary_margin: How far, in logical pixels, the content may be panned past the viewer's edges: one number or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }` (default 0).
interactiveviewer.clip_behavior: How the content is clipped to the viewer: `"hardEdge"` (default), `"antiAlias"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
interactiveviewer.constrained: Lays the content out at the viewer's size (default `true`); `false` lets large content keep its own size, for panning around a big image or map.
interactiveviewer.interaction_end_friction_coefficient: How quickly a fling slows down after the user lets go (default 0.0000135); a larger value stops it sooner.
interactiveviewer.interaction_update_interval: Minimum time between two `on_interaction_update` events, in milliseconds (default 200).
interactiveviewer.pan_enabled: Lets the user pan the content with a drag (default `true`).
interactiveviewer.scale_enabled: Lets the user zoom with a pinch or the mouse wheel (default `true`).
interactiveviewer.scale_factor: How much one mouse wheel step zooms (default 200); a smaller value zooms faster.
interactiveviewer.on_interaction_end: Fired when the user lets go; `event.data` has the keys `:pc` (the pointer count) and `:v`, the velocity as `{ x:, y: }` in pixels per second.
interactiveviewer.on_interaction_start: Fired when the user starts to pan or zoom; `event.data` has the keys `:lfp` and `:gfp` (the local and global focal point as `{ x:, y: }`) and `:pc` (the pointer count).
interactiveviewer.on_interaction_update: Fired as the user pans or zooms, at most once per `interaction_update_interval`; `event.data` has the keys `:s` (the scale since the start), `:rot`, `:fpd` (the focal point movement), `:lfp`, `:gfp` and `:pc`.

intrinsicheight.content: The control to size to its own intrinsic height; the first positional argument sets it.

intrinsicwidth.content: The control to size to its own intrinsic width; the first positional argument sets it.
intrinsicwidth.step_height: Rounds the height up to a multiple of this value, in logical pixels.
intrinsicwidth.step_width: Rounds the width up to a multiple of this value, in logical pixels.

keyboardlistener.autofocus: Takes keyboard focus when the listener first shows. Without focus it receives no keys.
keyboardlistener.content: The control inside the listener; the first positional argument sets it.
keyboardlistener.include_semantics: Tells screen readers that the listener can take focus (default `true`).
keyboardlistener.on_key_down: Fired when a key is pressed; `event.data[:key]` is its label, such as `"A"`, `"Enter"` or `"Arrow Up"`.
keyboardlistener.on_key_repeat: Fired while a held key repeats; `event.data[:key]` is its label.
keyboardlistener.on_key_up: Fired when a key is released; `event.data[:key]` is its label.

listview.animate_changes: Animates items that `page.update` adds or removes, as `item_animation` says (default `false`).
listview.item_animation: How `animate_changes` animates added and removed items: `{ type:, duration:, curve: }`, where `type` is `"fade"`, `"size"`, `"fade_size"` (default) or `"slide"` and `duration` defaults to 250 milliseconds.
listview.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh indicator. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
listview.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
listview.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull to start a refresh. iOS and macOS only.
listview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels (default 0).
listview.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` is a hash with the keys `:event_type` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `:pixels`, `:min_scroll_extent`, `:max_scroll_extent` and `:viewport_dimension`, plus `:scroll_delta` on updates, `:direction` on user events, and `:overscroll` and `:velocity` on overscroll.

markdown.auto_follow_links: Opens tapped links in the browser (default `false`); `on_tap_link` fires either way.
markdown.auto_follow_links_target: Where `auto_follow_links` opens a link on the web, for example `"_blank"` for a new tab.
markdown.code_style_sheet: Text styles for code blocks, in the same form as `md_style_sheet`.
markdown.code_theme: Syntax highlighting theme for code blocks: a theme name such as `"atom-one-dark"`, `"github"` or `"monokai-sublime"`, or a hash of token styles.
